#176960. MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest problem with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat.
  • MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.
  • Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest problem with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker says it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

It has been revealed that the result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

In a recent development, the single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker states that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

According to recent reports, there’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also promptly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Recent findings suggest that qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I noted in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

It has been revealed that at his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

According to recent reports, “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

Industry observers note that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, fresh signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If your soundbar just hasn't been making your movies sound as cinematic as they deserve, then perhaps it's time you entered the world of the home theater with one of the best AV receivers.

That's how you get the best surround experience possible, after all. If you're willing to invest in some speakers as well. One per channel, of course. We never said it would be cheap.

It has been revealed that our favorite amplifier at the moment is the Denon AVR-X4800H. It's an excellent performer with loads of great features, and doesn't cost as much as similar options. or if you need something that handle any format you throw at it, I'd recommend the Marantz Cinema 50.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

A sonic tour de force, the X4800H is a home theater amplifier with long-term appeal. The provision of a full board of 8K/4K 120Hz HDMI inputs, and coverage of all the significant home cinema sound formats, ensures that this Denon amp will partner any display or source you might acquire for a long time to come.

It's not the smallest box, but that's because it's fill with loads of amplification tech, supporting nine channels for massive surround sound or an Atmos system. The screen on the front makes it easy to read what mode its in, and then there's an easy setup mode when you plug it into your TV or projector. From there, you can setup all of the different settings and features to get the most out of your receiver.

The sound is powerful enough to make the experience feel almost physical. The soundstage is crisp and detailed, but there is a sense of power and precision as well; directional panning is totally convincing. While Denon rates on-board power at 9x 125W (into 8 Ohms) / 200W (into 6 Ohms), it sounds rather more muscular than that.

In a recent development, you'll get the most out of this amplifier while watching movies, especially those with detailed sound effects and soundtracks. But this also makes it a great companion for music, with your favorite tracks coming out of the two-channel stereo sounding light and agile, with immersive 3D audio mixes.

Industry observers note that the Marantz Cinema 50 is one of the most future-proof home theater amps we've seen. The connectivity on offer is truly impressive with 8K and 4K 120Hz support, 6 HDMI inputs plus three outputs, and an impressive auto calibration system.

Format support is extensive with Dolby Atmos, DTS:X and Auro 3D capable, as well as Sony’s 360 Reality Audio. It’s also IMAX Enhanced certified, which is a great advantage if you like to stream movies on Disney+, after the tech giant introduced IMAX audio mixes for select movies (including a lot of Marvel) in mid-2024.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for an AV amp that can deliver massive dynamics, with whip-crack fast transients and a fearsome bass extension, the Cinema 50 doesn’t disappoint. It’s a tremendously exciting listen and steers gunfire shootouts beautifully, with effortless panning, and even at high volume there's no hint of strain.

It has been revealed that it does music well too. Marantz’s lauded HDAM amplification circuitry is warm and melodious. In 2-channel mode, we’d say the Cinema 50 is comparable to a high-quality mid-range stereo amp, and with strong format support is as future-proof as they come right now.

The Marantz Cinema 70S is a half-height lifestyle AV receiver perfect for smaller spaces and viewing rooms. The sonic signature has a warm sound that works with hi-res audio as well as movies and gamers.

Recent findings suggest that you can run a 5.1.2 Atmos setup with a uniform 50W delivered across all 7 channels and it was peerless with movie soundtracks. In "Army of Thieves" (Dolby Atmos, Netflix), our reviewer really got the sense that they were travelling into the inner mechanism of the safe when Ludwig Dieter lays his hands on the lock, during the safecracking competition. The clicky travel of the dial is crisply delineated against the symphonic score, which rises all around.

Sources indicate that hooked up to a Fire TV stick listening to Dolby Atmos music mixes from Tidal, our reviewer was thrilled at just how seamlessly the 360 presentation was. Billy Porter’s "Break A Sweat" places the listener firmly in the middle of the dance floor, with horns in the surround, the vocal dead center and the main beat gyrating across the LCR.

In our 5.1.2 configuration, there were no sonic gaps or dips with any kind of content, just a totally immersive listening experience.

When testing models for inclusion in our best AV receivers page, we play a range of media, including movies, music and games, to evaluate overall sound quality performance.

Industry observers note that we also test any companion software that may come with an AV receiver, and factor in how easy it is to set up and use each receiver with a reference speaker system. Other features we consider include the different kinds of connectivity options, all of which determine how well it will work with your home entertainment setup.

We also take into account power output, the number of supported audio channels and subwoofer outputs, and available processing software for decoding movie soundtracks as well as their ability to handle music sources — all factors that greatly affect how each speaker will sound in your living room.

According to recent reports, an AV receiver is an amplifier that's designed for home cinema and movie watching. You plug it into your TV with an HDMI cable, and then it takes the audio signal, and processes it for separate speakers. You need to have speakers for an AV receiver to work — it's a kind of go-between device.

According to recent reports, you could have as many speakers as you like, although there's a minimum of two. Everything from a normal stereo (two speakers) up to a much larger surround setup (7.1 and above). It needs to be plugged into the power as well. Remember to budget for speakers with an AV receiver.

This is a big question to ask yourself. Do you have the space for multiple speakers around the room? What kind of watching do you do? Can you budget for more than two speakers?

According to recent reports, if the answer to any of those questions is no, then you don't need an AV receiver. I'd argue, in fact, that very few people need an AV receiver — you're much better off with the space-saving capabilities of one of the best soundbars, or the musical chops of a pair of HDMI-enabled powered speakers like the Kanto Ren.

But, if you love watching movies, you've got plenty of space, plenty of budget, and permission from your significant other, then an AV receiver might be just what you've been looking for.

Sources indicate that everyone's movie room is different. They're different shapes and have different furniture inside, which can affect the sound of your system. In order to make movies sound their best, no matter what's in your room, manufacturers have built room correction systems that listen to the sound and then compensate for the differences in decor and shape.

Some, like Denon and Yamaha, have made their own room correction systems built into companion apps. Many amplifiers come with microphones to aid the process, and its built into the setup of the device. It's well worth going through the stages, and it can make a big difference to bass extension and surround sound placement.

Industry observers note that yes, you can! And you most certainly should. Your AVR can be used as the central pillar of a home music system, especially as more and more devices can connect to whole-home music streaming devices. That means you can connect your turntable, CD player, or other devices.

In a recent development, for turntables, there are a couple of things to bear in mind. Some AVRs do not have a built-in phono pre-amp, and so you'll need either a separate device or a TT with a pre-amp built in. If your AVR has a built-in pre-amp, you'll need to make sure you connect your TT to the correct RCA plugs. They'll be labeled "phono.".

It has been revealed that they are good for gaming, though it depends on the types of games you like to play. For immersive RPGs filled with movie-like cutscenes and massive set pieces, you're in for a sonic treat. For fast-paced online shooters, you'll likely want to stick with your gaming headset.

Just make sure that your newly introduced AVR and your TV support HDMI 2.1 for the best audio and visual experience possible. That means that 4K120Hz will be supported, along with Variable refresh rates and other game-specific features can be supported.

Industry observers note that if you want to get the most out of the home theater experience, then you should pick up some Atmos speakers for the full effect. Without them, you won't get the spatial audio channels that make the sound come from above you — it's well worth it if you can stump up the cash.

Buying something as complex and multi-talented as an AV receiver can be overwhelming to a casual consumer, so if you’re serious about transforming your sound output into something more theater-like, start educating yourself on the necessities by familiarizing yourself with the things to consider.

Something to know right out of the gate is that most seven-channel AV receivers support a speaker configuration of 5.1.2, which is the standard 5.1 surround layout with two additional height/up-firing speakers. Models that feature nine channels of amplification can be used for either 5.1 with four Dolby height speakers (5.1.4) or 7.1 surround with two height channels (7.1.2). Speaker models such as those in the newly introduced Klipsch Reference series could make a great partnership for a home cinema setup, and has several upward-firing height speakers to meet Dolby Amos requirements.

In a recent development, finding the best AV receiver isn’t just about HDMI inputs. Sure we like plenty of inputs, but the number of outputs is notable too, particularly if you plan on running both a flatscreen and a projector in the same room.

If you're considering an AV receiver as a connectivity hub for a music system as well as movies, then be sure to check out our guide to the best turntables for any budget. Many of the receivers available today come with a built-in moving-magnet phono stage to enable vinyl playback from any of the record decks we've tested.

Resolution and frame rate support.

Do you need 8K or High Frame Rate HDMIs? If your AV receiver is unlikely to have a games console connected then the answer is no. In which case there are some great deals to be had on AVRs with regular HDMI 2.0 inputs.

In a recent development, dolby Atmos compatibility is a given (and by default that means you’ll get DTS:X too), but how many channels do you need? Given the option, 9 channels always trump 7, because it opens up more speaker options such as 5.1.4 or 7.1.2, for example.

Don’t have a full Dolby Atmos home theater loudspeaker setup? Look for a model that offers height virtualization technology, so you can enjoy an immersive audio experience even when you don’t have a full set of physical speakers.

Recent findings suggest that power isn’t just about roof-raising volume, and even if you’re not lucky enough to have a dedicated movie room, a model with major amplification makes sense. A high power output means an AVR can deliver dynamic transients, and pressure load a space without clipping or strain.

One of the most confusing things about any kind of home cinema system is the surround sound channel numbers you'll often spot on the box. What do they mean, and what do they tell you about the receiver that you're about to buy?

It has been revealed that those numbers denote the channels that are available to use with the receiver. It's broken up into three different sections. The first number is the surround channels. The middle is for subwoofers. The final number is the height channels, for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X.

Sources indicate that say, for example, that you've got a receiver that's got a 7.1.4 surround sound setup. That means you've got seven surround channels that you could use for a centre, left and right stereo, two side surrounds, and then a pair of rear surrounds. You've then got a single subwoofer channel.

According to recent reports, finally, you've got four height channels that you can place around the room in predetermined Atmos spots. You can use Atmos testing videos to make sure all your speakers are in the right place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei, chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, president.

Anthropic shares fell below their $83 IPO price for the first time on Tuesday. The company’s record Nasdaq debut was five days ago. The stock was down 5.4% at $82.78 in early trading, Medha Singh reported for Reuters. It opened at $111.50 on 19 November.

Sources indicate that later in the morning, the fall had reached 7%, CNBC reported. At Reuters’ price, Anthropic was worth about $1.5tn, roughly 40 times its sales over the past 12 months. On its first day, it touched $2tn.

Recent findings suggest that the stock closed 17% higher on that first day. Since then, a wider tech sell-off has hit the market. It pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory, Reuters noted. Anthropic also missed Monday’s AI rally after Nvidia brought Jensen Huang back as chief executive.

“If we do see a slowdown in the data-center buildout, then that obviously can impact the speed at which Anthropic can develop,” Fiona Cincotta of StoneX told Reuters.

In a recent development, reuters pointed to other large tech debuts that lost their early gains. SpaceX’s $85.7bn June listing was the biggest before Anthropic’s. It took about a month to fall below its offer price. Facebook, now Meta, did so on its second trading day in 2012.

“Like most IPOs, it probably came in overpriced and it is now the real price discovery,” Peter Andersen of Andersen Capital Management told Reuters.

Some support could come from index funds. MSCI will add Anthropic to its global standard indexes as of the 30 November close. Index analytics firm Intropic estimates that passive funds could buy up to 30% of the shares offered by the end of the year.

Recent findings suggest that chief executive Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei each sold more than 3.37m shares, worth over $280m. They sold them to the IPO’s underwriters a day after the debut, according to a filing late on Monday. The sales were part of the founders’ planned sale, in which all seven co-founders offered 3,378,378 shares each.

Industry observers note that anthropic’s lock-up rules let some employees and insiders sell part of their holdings from the first trading day. Further releases are tied to earnings reports. The underwriters also used their option to buy extra shares. That lifted the offering to $93.5bn when Anthropic closed the offering. Reuters noted that it also removed a possible source of support for the stock.

Recent findings suggest that reuters also listed cheaper open-weight models as a risk, such as those from DeepSeek, Mistral and Moonshot AI. Anthropic has warned that they could pressure its prices. Huang is a strong supporter of open-weight models.

It has been revealed that three brokers started coverage with positive ratings, CNBC reported. Canaccord Genuity rated the stock a buy with a $135 target. Its analysts noted Anthropic is building:.

“One of the most notable enterprise technology franchises of the AI era.”.

Sources indicate that oppenheimer set an outperform rating and a $150 target on Tuesday, citing enterprise AI spending and Anthropic’s compute efficiency. On Monday, Wedbush started at outperform with a $120 target.

“The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme,” the Wedbush analysts wrote.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the best all-in-one printer should make everyday jobs simpler, whether you're printing shipping labels, scanning notable paperwork, copying forms or producing color photos at home. The right choice depends on what you print and how often: some models prioritise rapid document handling, while others keep ink costs down or deliver stronger photo output.

Sources indicate that our tested picks cover each of those needs, from the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II being a capable all-rounder for most households to low-cost options like the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW. There's even the Inkwon Tag, a compact creative printer for stickers and creating custom T-shirts.

Industry observers note that at Tom's Guide, we test each printer for printing speeds, print quality, ink costs and more. Read on to find the model that best matches your workload, budget and must-have features, including scanning, copying and faxing.

Printers might not be the most impressive (or interesting) things in the world, but they are supremely useful. To make sure you get the best printer possible, our dedicated reviews team put printers through their paces. That's going to be Nikita Achanta, on the Tom's Guide side, who's been testing consumer electronics for years. Then there are our freelancers, such as Eric Butterfield, who's tested a range of brands.

These are the tests that we put the printers through so that we can properly evaluate their performance.

With the amount of shipping labels I need printed and documents that need copying for my household, a printer has become a quiet essential for my home. That's why I wanted a simple, do-it-all machine, and I refer to our experts, Nikita Achanta and Eric Butterfield, for all the in-depth recommendations they have to offer.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

When it comes down to it, the Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is quite simply the only printer you'll ever need. Yes, it can print, scan, copy and fax, but it does it all with a hassle-free setup experience and rapid speeds across the board. When a printer actually gives easy step-by-step instructions on how to fix a paper jam, you know it's a good one.

In our tests, it delivered a five-page text print job in just 11.31 seconds (26.5 pages per minute) and scanned in color in 6.22 seconds, and that's faster than its inkjet competitors.

And this 250-capacity printer (plus an extra 150 prints in the middle section) has quick start-up, too, as our reviewer, Nikita, found it effortless to get up and running, with warm-up times as quick as 14 seconds from off.

It isn't just speed, as print quality is consistently sharp and detailed, both in color and black and white, and everyday jobs came out looking just as sharp as they did on our screens. Where the MF753Cdw II pulls ahead of inkjet competitors like the more budget-friendly Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is in raw speed and features.

You get much faster printing and a true all-in-one experience (there's no faxing on the G3290), but running costs are higher if you print in volume. Against the business-class Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850, the MF753Cdw II still keeps up on print speed and quality but can’t match those rock-bottom ink costs.

That’s the main compromise here: the per-page price is higher than what you’ll find with most ink tank printers (around 5.1 cents per color page and 2.7 cents per mono print). But not by that much, and that shouldn't put you off grabbing this workhorse.

If you want a dependable, fuss-free machine for everyday tasks — letters, homework, invoices, you name it — the MF753Cdw II is the best fit for most households.

In a recent development, unless you need faxing in your life, this is the all-in-one printer to grab if you're after a reliable machine for excellent prints. The Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW stands out largely thanks to its exceptionally low ink costs: just 0.3 cents per black page and 0.94 cents per color page based on our lab testing. That's value you can't ignore.

According to recent reports, in daily use, the T780DW keeps pace with demanding routines. It prints standard text documents at 12.4 pages per minute (ppm) and handles double-sided text at 6.7 ppm. These speeds put it among the fastest inkjets we've tested for both single and duplex jobs, making it reliable for everything from schoolwork to business invoices.

It has been revealed that print and scan quality are equally reassuring. In our hands-on tests, text and graphics came out crisp and accurate, while color scans preserved detail and clarity.

It has been revealed that the main compromise is its 20-sheet automatic document feeder. While fine for light multi-page copying and scanning, if you've got a large batch of documents, it will take some time to do. That, and there's no USB thumb drive port, and don't expect to make double-sided copies or scans via the automatic document feeder (ADF).

In any case, for those who want low running costs and easy printing, the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW will fit in nicely with your home or office.

Whether you're a photographer or just need highly detailed, colorful prints, the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is the all-in-one printer for you. Sure, it may come with fewer additional features, but it excels where it matters: print quality and affordability.

It's a modest printer; it has just one paper tray and no document feeder, and it's not the speediest option. But for home use, it's an excellent choice. Expect this to deliver reliable, high-quality prints with the versatility to do documents, photos and double-sided print jobs. Speaking of which, those graphic prints and glossy photos will come out with plenty of detail and natural, accurate colors.

Sources indicate that while the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 prints at pretty average speeds, it actually excels at double-sided documents. In our testing, it printed single-sided pages at an average of 9.2 pages per minute, but double-sided text documents cranked up to 7.2 pages per minute, the fastest duplex print speed we've recorded of any recent ink tank printers.

And thanks to its easy setup process, robust wireless support (this thing can print via Wi-Fi or a smartphone app) and low ink costs (we estimate color prints cost roughly 0.9 cents per page, significantly lower than the 1.9 cents per page category average), I recommend the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 for anyone seeking an affordable, reliable ink all-in-one printer, especially for photo printing.

If your at-home office needs fast, reliable color printing day in and day out, the Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850 is just the printer you'll want. In our tests, it handled a six-page mixed color document in just 1 minute and 8 seconds (5.3 pages per minute), nearly doubling the category average, so you won’t be waiting on significant print jobs during busy stretches.Where the ET-5850 really stands out for speedy work prints is its speed with graphics-heavy jobs. Letter-size glossy photos print in 2 minutes and 21 seconds, far outpacing typical inkjets. The three separate paper input trays mean you can keep letter, legal, and specialty papers ready to go, which helps minimize interruptions if multiple people are printing different document types.

Sources indicate that moreover, you're getting an impressively low ink costs with a device capable of handling more than 3,000 pages per month. During our testing, we found an extremely low per-page cost of 0.4 cents for text pages, and 1.6 cents per color page. The printer can scan, copy and fax, uses dual 250-page paper cassettes and has a 50-sheet automatic document feeder.

Recent findings suggest that setup was mostly straightforward, but we did run into some hiccups. Connecting to our network required manually entering a router password (WPS isn’t supported), and the touchscreen flagged network issues before resolving. Once added, using the printer with a Mac was simple, but it’s worth noting you might spend extra time on initial setup and troubleshooting.If you’re after an all-in-one that keeps pace with high-volume, graphics-rich business tasks and want flexible paper handling, the ET-5850 is a great fit.

Alright, this one's a little different from any other all-in-one printer, as the Inkwon Tag is a one-of-a-kind portable color inkjet printer. Instead of printing, scanning or copying documents, this pocketable printer delivers all the fun stuff — instant photo prints for scrapbooks, heat transfers for creating custom T-shirts, temporary tattoos and even stickers.

This 4-in-1 portable printer is as tiny as it is light, coming in at 4.1 x 3.8 x 1.7 inches and weighing just 8.2 ounces. Our reviewer, Nikita, has no problems carrying this around in a pocket, as it's actually smaller than the best major phones around today.

Despite its size, you'll find it boasts surprisingly good print quality, no matter the image. It uses a CMY three-dye-based ink system (no dedicated black ink, though) with a resolution of 600 dpi, making it excellent for small prints of friends and loved ones, designs of your choosing or even screenshots from games. And it's all extremely easy to use, right from setting it up to the very user-friendly app for editing and printing photos.

In a recent development, it isn't perfect, as it can only handle one sheet of paper at a time, and don't expect it to create any borderless prints. It's also quite a pricey portable printer, coming in at $299, but its ink costs and paper refills are much more value-friendly when compared to its competition, especially from Canon or Instax (plus, those brands don't offer 4-in-1 portable printer options with sticker or heat transfer capabilities).

It has been revealed that to have a mini, portable printer by your side to instantly create stickers to personalize whatever you want, temporary tattoos for parties, heat transfers for customized T-shirts and Polaroid-like photos, all at low running ink costs? As far as portable all-in-one printers go, the Inkwon Tag is a winner.

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a compact, capable printer purely for stickers and photo prints, then the StickerPix Print + Cut is exactly what you're after. It comes in an adorable design, is fast at printing stickers and offers loads of templates to customize what you want to print. There are only 18 sheets of sticker/photo paper out of the box, so you'll need to invest in more, and the Inkwon Tag offers a bit more "all-in-one" versatility, but the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut is well worth grabbing for all things stickers! Read our full Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut review.

(★★★★☆)The Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW bucked the trend of printers gouging you on ink costs by coming with roughly a year's worth of ink (depending on how much you print) pre-loaded in the extra-large ink cartridges, so you get a great price-per-page right out of the gate. On top of that, the Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW offers solid printing, scanning and copying. But this model is trickier to find these days, and more of the current Brother printers of its kind do just the job for less these days. Read our full Brother INKvestment MFC-J995DW review.

It has been revealed that (★★★★☆½)The Brother MFC-L2750DW XL is the best multifunction laser printer we've reviewed in years for everything but color prints. Every print is sharp and clean, and it's packed with features including a quick ADF, fast duplex printing and copying, fax capability, and a second paper tray. But this is one pricey machine!Read our full Brother MFC-L2750DW XL review.

According to recent reports, (★★★★☆)Looking for another photo printer option? The Canon Pixma TR8620 is a fantastic shout that offers plenty of office features, from scanning and faxing to a 20-page ADF, a duplexer for two-sided printing, and two paper trays for keeping two types of paper at the ready. But that extra ink cartridge does bump up the cost of ink. Read our full Canon Pixma TR8620 review.

According to recent reports, to help you find the best all-in-one printer, we put each model through an extensive range of printer tests, including timed prints of text, mixed text and graphics and color photos. The resulting prints are carefully examined for errors and issues, and compared with samples from other printers to determine the print quality.

We time every test print to see how rapidly the machine handles document printing, and closely examine the finished product to determine how well different printing tasks are handled.

We also test the scanning and copying functions of the printer, timing how promptly it captures a page and comparing the results to the original images to determine how well it captures color and detail.

To measure the cost of owning and operating a printer, we look at the current street price of ink refills and the estimated number of pages that each cartridge can produce, and calculate the cost of printing a single page.

Not sure which all-in-one printer to buy? Obviously, you want a printer that performs well, so all of our reviews and rankings discuss a printer's output quality and speed, but there's more to an all-in-one printer than just how swiftly it can crank out documents.

Some companies even offer subscription services that save you money while sending you ink just in time to replace that empty cartridge. Learn more in our article HP Instant Ink vs. Canon vs. Epson: Are ink subscriptions worth it?

Ink-tank printers, a type of Inkjet, usually offer the lowest running costs because their refill bottles deliver far more pages than conventional cartridges.

In our guide, the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW is the best-value option for home or light-office use, while the Epson EcoTank Pro ET-5850 pairs very low per-page costs with the capacity and features needed for heavier business printing.

You should compare current cost-per-page figures with your expected print volume, not just the printer’s upfront price.

It has been revealed that choose an inkjet if you print color graphics or photos, want a lower upfront price or value the low ongoing costs of an ink-tank model. Choose a laser all-in-one if your priority is fast, sharp text documents and a responsive office workflow.

The Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is our top pick, as it's a fast laser workhorse, whereas the Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290 is the stronger fit for photo printing.

An automatic document feeder (ADF) is worthwhile if you regularly scan, copy or fax multi-page documents, as it feeds the sheets for you instead of requiring one page at a time on the scanner glass.

Sources indicate that it matters less for occasional household printing or photo-focused use. Also check its capacity and whether it supports double-sided scanning: an ADF does not automatically mean both sides can be scanned in one pass.

Recent findings suggest that some can, but not every all-in-one printer with an ADF supports automatic double-sided scanning or copying. Do not confuse duplex printing with duplex scanning: a printer may print on both sides of a sheet while still requiring you to turn over originals when scanning or copying.

Check the model’s specifications before buying; the Brother INKvestment MFC-T780DW has an ADF but does not support duplex scanning or copying through it.

Sources indicate that many current all-in-one printers support wireless mobile printing through a manufacturer app, Apple AirPrint or another built-in service. The Canon MegaTank Pixma G3290, for example, supports Wi-Fi and printing through a smartphone app.

Before buying, confirm that the printer works with your phone or tablet, operating system, preferred app and network setup. Some features may require the device and printer to be on the same Wi-Fi network.

IBM Consulting’s cyber chief tells companies to assume failure as AI speeds up attacks

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mark Hughes, Global Managing Partner, Cybersecurity Services, IBM Consulting.
  • Attackers now move at machine speed, but most companies still fix their systems at human speed.
  • Recent findings suggest that hughes leads IBM Consulting’s cybersecurity business worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Hughes, Global Managing Partner, Cybersecurity Services, IBM Consulting.

Attackers now move at machine speed, but most companies still fix their systems at human speed. That is the view of Mark Hughes, Global Managing Partner of Cybersecurity Services at IBM Consulting.

Recent findings suggest that hughes leads IBM Consulting’s cybersecurity business worldwide. Before IBM, he was president of security at DXC Technology and chief executive of BT Security. He spoke to TNW by email, after a run of US outages and AI-found flaws in widely used software.

AI is helping attackers automate large parts of an attack, Hughes mentioned. That covers researching targets, finding weaknesses, and building and refining the attack itself. Agentic AI could let them automate even more of that process.

“We’re not at a point where every attack is autonomous or even AI-driven, but organizations should blueprint for and anticipate this to accelerate in the coming year,” he stated.

According to The Washington Sun, bank chief executives and the NSA have told Congress about the recent US outages. They blamed rushed patches for flaws found by AI, as we reported on 18 November. The Trump administration denies any link between the outages.

Hughes did not comment on the outages themselves. AI is making vulnerabilities “incredibly easy” to find, for defenders and attackers alike, he stated. The major gap is remediation, which still depends on engineering context, testing, validation and coordinated development.

“So we have attackers moving at machine speed, finding and chaining vulnerabilities into viable attack paths, while businesses are still largely remediating at human speed,” Hughes said.

Sources indicate that “The answer isn’t to just patch everything faster. You need to understand which vulnerabilities actually create the most risk to your specific environment, and prioritize those, while making sure the fix itself doesn’t disrupt the systems organizations depend on,” he stated.

Hughes did not say how many IBM clients are struggling with the volume of fixes. He pointed instead to Lightwell. IBM and Red Hat revealed the programme on 28 May. It is a $5bn commitment backed by more than 20,000 engineers.

It has been revealed that lightwell combines AI with engineering expertise to identify, validate and fix vulnerabilities in foundational open source software, Hughes mentioned. That includes versions already running inside complex company systems. It aims to deliver validated fixes that organisations can use in active workflows.

In October, IBM and Red Hat gave an revision. Lightwell had found and fixed more than 400 previously unknown vulnerabilities in widely used Java libraries, they stated. IBM also prepares to bring Anthropic’s Claude Mythos to enterprise customers.

According to recent reports, open source matters so much now because the critical infrastructure people rely on every day runs on it, Hughes remarked. That ranges from banking and healthcare to transportation.

“That widespread reliance also heightens the stakes when something goes wrong,” he noted.

In a recent development, AI is speeding up discovery, and fixes are not keeping pace, he added. Many open source projects still rely on volunteers, he stated, and that explains part of the gap. They have few resources to match the upcoming speed of threats.

Asked what one change a defender should make this quarter, Hughes noted: “Assume failure.” He pointed to the outages that hit critical infrastructure organisations in quick succession. He also pointed to flaws in widely used software such as PHP, uncovered at unprecedented scale. Attackers are already exploiting the PHP2Shell flaws, the US cyber agency CISA confirmed in October.

It has been revealed that “You still want to prevent as many attacks as possible, but no organization can stop every attack, outage or software problem. Disruption is going to happen. What matters is how prepared you are when something goes wrong,” Hughes stated.

Organisations need to be ready for systems to fail, he remarked. The cause might be an attack, a software problem or something else.

According to recent reports, hughes expects 2027 to extend what this year has brought. Attack cycles will keep speeding up as more capable AI becomes easier to get. He also expects more vulnerability discoveries and more automation across attacks.

Sources indicate that companies are also scaling their use of autonomous agents, he said. That brings a whole new set of risks around identity, access and control.

To keep pace, he stated, companies will need to change how they run security.

“Organizations are going to have to reimagine their security operations, moving towards autonomous security, while also making sure the agents acting on their behalf have the proper controls in place to prevent unintended behaviors,” he remarked.

In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Stalw

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook.
  • It has been revealed that stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover.
  • Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange.

It has been revealed that stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover. Outlook, Apple Mail and the mail apps on phones and tablets connect to Stalwart as they would to an Exchange server, with mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes in one account. Users type their email address and password, Autodiscover does the rest, and they keep working in the client they already know.

Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL.

Before going into what Stalwart now does, it is worth looking at where self-hosted Exchange stands today, because it explains why so many organisations are looking for a way out.

According to recent reports, microsoft has not announced the end of Exchange Server. On paper, on-premises Exchange still exists. In practice, every road Microsoft is building leads to Exchange Online:.

Industry observers note that none of these steps forces anyone to move on its own. Together, they leave an Exchange administrator with a shrinking set of choices: keep running a server that will not grow, or move the organisation’s mail into Microsoft’s cloud.

According to recent reports, for many organisations the second option is not acceptable. Email is the record of a company’s contracts, negotiations, legal advice, HR matters and customer data. Placing it with a US provider means placing it within reach of US law, including the CLOUD Act, which allows US authorities to compel American providers to hand over data they control wherever it is stored. Public administrations, healthcare providers, law firms, defence contractors and many European companies cannot accept that, or no longer want to. Data sovereignty means that you decide where your data lives, under which jurisdiction, and who can read it. A mail service in someone else’s cloud cannot offer that, and an on-premises server whose vendor is steering its customers toward that cloud offers less of it every year.

The obstacle to leaving Exchange has rarely been the server. It has been the client.

Many people have spent their whole working life in Outlook. They have years of muscle memory in it: their folder layout, their rules, their calendar views, their shared mailboxes, the way they book meeting rooms. Many organisations also have workflows built around it, such as delegated calendars managed by an assistant. Replacing Exchange with a standard IMAP and CalDAV server has always meant telling every one of those people to switch to a different mail client, or to reconfigure Outlook into a reduced IMAP mode where calendars and contacts no longer sync. For a migration project, that is often where the blueprint dies.

With Stalwart 1.2.0 the users do not need to change anything. The administrator moves the mailboxes and points the DNS records at Stalwart, and users connect with the same Outlook they used before.

Stalwart implements the following Microsoft protocols, all served on the same HTTPS port as JMAP and the WebUI:.

That set of protocols is what the following clients use to talk to an Exchange server, and they can connect to Stalwart the same way:.

The Exchange protocols are not a separate silo inside Stalwart. They are another door into the same accounts. A message filed in Outlook is in the same mailbox an IMAP or JMAP client sees, a meeting accepted on a phone appears in the calendar that CalDAV clients read, and a contact added in Apple Contacts demonstrates up in the CardDAV address book. A user can keep Outlook on the office desktop, the native mail app on a phone and a JMAP webmail in the browser, all on one account.

Recent findings suggest that rules created in Outlook’s Rules and Alerts are stored on the server as mail rules, which run as Sieve when the message is delivered. They apply when Outlook is closed and whatever client the user opens next. Delegates and folder permissions set in Outlook become regular Stalwart shares, so they apply to every protocol. Shared mailboxes open automatically in Outlook from group membership, as they do with Exchange.

Industry observers note that not every part of an Exchange deployment has a counterpart. Stalwart does not offer public folders, archive mailboxes, mobile device management, RPC over HTTP (Outlook 2010 and earlier) or NTLM and Kerberos sign-in: clients authenticate with a password, an app password or OAuth. The Exchange documentation covers configuration, DNS and Autodiscover, each family of clients, and the differences from Exchange that administrators should know about before a migration.

One Outlook is missing from the list above: the upcoming Outlook for Windows, the one that Windows now installs by default and that classic Outlook keeps offering through a toggle in its title bar.

According to recent reports, the fresh Outlook does not work with Stalwart, and it does not work with any self-hosted server, Exchange included. It is built to work through Microsoft’s cloud. Microsoft does not support on-premises Exchange accounts in it at all.

According to recent reports, the new Outlook does accept IMAP accounts, and that might look like a way around the problem. It is not. When an IMAP account is added to the new Outlook, the connection to the mail server is not made from the user’s computer. As heise and c’t reported in November 2023, the new Outlook sends the IMAP server name, the user name and the password to Microsoft, and Microsoft’s cloud connects to the mail server on the user’s behalf. Every message then passes through Microsoft’s infrastructure on its way to the screen. Microsoft does not only see the mail; it holds the password to the mailbox.

It has been revealed that for an organisation that runs its own mail server to keep its data under its own control, this defeats the purpose of the whole exercise. We advise against using the new Outlook with any self-hosted email deployment, whether it runs Stalwart or anything else. People who see the “Try the new Outlook” toggle in classic Outlook should leave it off.

Industry observers note that the same applies on phones. Outlook for iOS and Android reach on-premises mailboxes through a Microsoft cloud service as well, which requires a hybrid Exchange Online setup. On mobile devices, the native mail, calendar and contacts apps, which connect directly over ActiveSync, are the better choice.

The obvious question is why Stalwart is adding Exchange protocols now. EWS is being removed from Exchange Online, Microsoft’s own future for Outlook is a cloud client, and classic Outlook is reportedly supported until 2029. Why build support for protocols that will be obsolete in a few years?

Because the companies that run Exchange today cannot wait a few years, and because those protocols are the bridge they need to cross.

In a recent development, an organisation with a few hundred Outlook users cannot replace its mail server and its mail client in the same weekend. It can replace the server, though, if nobody notices. With Stalwart speaking the Exchange protocols, the server moves first: mailboxes are migrated, DNS records change, and on Monday every user opens the same Outlook and the same phone apps they used on Friday. The organisation’s mail is back under its own control from day one, and no one’s work is interrupted to get there.

Industry observers note that the client can then change at the pace that suits the owners. Over time, as classic Outlook reaches the end of its life and the new Outlook remains tied to Microsoft’s cloud, we expect users to move gradually to third-party email clients built on open standards, and in particular on JMAP. Outlook will stop being an option for anyone who cares about where their email lives, and by then the people who used it will have had the time to choose something else without a deadline over their heads.

Industry observers note that exchange support is not where Stalwart is going. It is how organisations get from where they are to where Stalwart is.

Exchange compatibility is not a small piece of work. It adds about 200,000 lines of code to Stalwart, and we know that some of you would rather not carry that weight if you never proposal to see an Outlook client. We built it with that in mind, so that it costs as little as possible for those who do not use it, and so that it can be removed cleanly once the Exchange protocols are obsolete:.

A drop-in replacement is only useful if the data can follow. Vandelay, our account import and export tool, migrates mailboxes from both sides of Microsoft’s offering:.

Vandelay copies each account into Stalwart over JMAP, and the domain moves to Stalwart when its MX records and client settings change. The migration guide for hosted services walks through the whole process, from the first test account to the cutover. With the Exchange protocols enabled on Stalwart, Outlook and the other Exchange clients then connect through Autodiscover and find the migrated mail, calendars and contacts.

Exchange support is the headline, but 1.2.0 brings several other features, most of them developed alongside it because an Exchange replacement needs them:.

The changelog lists every change and fix, along with the upgrade steps: existing servers need to add the fresh permissions to their default roles.

Last week we also released version 2.0.0 of stalwart-cli, and its biggest addition is an interactive console. Run stalwart-cli with no arguments in a terminal and it opens a full-screen interface that covers the same ground as the WebUI: browsing and editing accounts, domains and every other configuration object, watching the dashboard, following live traces and running actions. It is aimed at administrators who live in SSH sessions, or who work on hosts where opening a browser is impractical.

It has been revealed that the console is built with Ratatui, the excellent Rust library for terminal user interfaces, and it is schema-driven like the rest of the CLI: its screens, forms and field help come from the schema that the server publishes, so it picks up latest objects without being updated. The CLI also learned to sign in with the OAuth device flow and to remember the session, so a single approval in the browser is enough for both the console and every subsequent command.

Stalwart will be at FOSDEM 2027 in Brussels. We will have a Stalwart stand, and on Saturday, 30 January 2027, we will give a talk about moving from Microsoft Exchange to Stalwart in the Modern Email devroom. If you are planning a migration away from Exchange, or are curious about what it takes, come and talk to us. We will post the time and title of the talk once the schedule is published.

Until then, the Exchange documentation has everything needed to try it, and we would love to hear how your Outlook clients get on with Stalwart.

Earlier this season, he was involved in a furious altercation with rival officials in the tunnel.

In August, he was involved in a furious altercation with Remo officials after Santos beat them in the last 16 of the Brazilian Cup.

The Brazilian football icon screamed inside the tunnel as he was drawn into a heated exchange with Remo's directors.

He repeatedly shouted the word 'eliminated' before taunting the rivals with a series of gestures at his dressing room's entrance.

Despite his bragging over other teams, it has been a distinctly average campaign for Santos so far.

Santos sit eighth in the Brazilian Serie A and, despite him telling Coritiba that they will go down, that looks unlikely with the southern side sat 13th out of 20 with four games to go, four points above the drop zone.

Meanwhile, while he mocked Remo over being eliminated from the cup, Santos went out in the quarter-finals 3-0 on aggregate to Palmeiras.

Neymar has had a fairly effective season personally, scoring 10 goals and recording eight assists in all competitions while captaining Santos.

It remains to be seen whether he will play beyond the end of his contract in December, but the club's chief executive, who happens to be Neymar's dad, certainly wants to extend his son's term.

'We know that in every transfer window, offers come in for him to leave. Yet Neymar always chooses to stay at Santos. What I'm anticipating is that, first and foremost, I need to keep Neymar happy. Do you understand?' he said.

It has been revealed that 'And if he's happy here, I can keep him here. So, look, down this final stretch, the work we've done to structure the squad and open up positive possibilities has given us the license to dream.'.

Neymar, who was widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation during his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, returned to his boyhood club Santos from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in January 2025.

His £200million move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain remains the most expensive transfer of all time.

In June he made his first appearance for Brazil since 2023 after rupturing his ACL and meniscus in his left knee.

Recent findings suggest that claude Ship is a new product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

According to recent reports, “That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic claims. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. “Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the fresh /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic claims.

💡 Key Takeaways
