iPad Air vs iPad Pro: Which should you buy?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro.
  • Bonus pick: The all-upcoming iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.
  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-upcoming iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

Industry observers note that the iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

Industry observers note that the iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

In a recent development, the biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

In a recent development, contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

According to recent reports, for most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

Recent findings suggest that the iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Recent findings suggest that still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

Aberdeen's new manager is a proven overachiever with a significant personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.

Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event. While unquestionably a successful manager with Motherwell and St Mirren, there was always a lingering doubt about whether his skill set would work at a bigger club with different expectations in terms of style of play. And so it proved.

What didn’t help the Northern Irishman was the perception that those who employed him weren’t exactly bowled over by him in the first place, either.

Robinson would have been a hard enough sell to the Dons support had he been unveiled a few days after Jimmy Thelin departed the scene in January.

That it took them 67 days to deliver confirmation of the appointment – after the club had dalliances with Eirik Horneland and Sandro Schwarz – was hardly a ringing endorsement of their faith in him.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast with the process to appoint Mario Frick is striking. Robinson was sacked two days after a four-goal home thrashing by Hibernian. Five days later, the former Liechtenstein international was named by the Pittodrie club as the new head coach.

It has been revealed that after the saga at the start of the year which reflected well on no one, Aberdeen, to give them their dues, knew what they wanted and saw Frick as a hand-in-glove fit. So, what led them so rapidly to his door?

Mario Frick is unveiled at Pittodrie and immediately vowed to transform the club's fortunes.

The 52-year-old, essentially, is a head coach who fits in with the overarching strategy Aberdeen identified several years ago.

This has been lost along the way as poor results have seen a churn of individuals occupy the dug-out, many of whom were square pegs in round holes. This, the club believe, has been why the recruitment has been so random and ineffective.

There’s been little joined-up thinking, as evidenced by the summer window which saw 15 players arrive, many of whom were sub-standard or clearly not part of Robinson’s proposal.

The intention always was for the head coach to work in tandem with the sporting director and chief executive rather than independently of them.

While Frick will have a say on what players arrive and depart this January, the conversations around the identity of the team and what’s required to improve it will be three-way.

At Luzern, Frick was happy to trust the judgment of director of football Remo Meyer on such matters.

His willingness to forge the same relationship with Aberdeen’s sporting director, Lutz Pfannenstiel, was the light bulb moment for chief executive Adrian Bevington and chairman Dave Cormack.

Frick earned 125 caps for Liechtenstein and scored 16 goals for the European minnows.

Recent findings suggest that in keeping with the much-vaunted ‘continental’ model, Pfannenstiel and head of recruitment Darren Mowbray will largely identify players to fit the system. Frick will then be tasked with making it all work.

The blueprint is for the squad to be closely aligned with the head coach’s needs rather than assembling the rag bag of players who’ve come in the three windows since Thelin won the Scottish Cup.

There’s much beyond Frick’s willingness to defer matters of player identification to others which caught the eye of the board, however.

Although very much a modern and forward-thinking coach, he’s vastly experienced in the game.

As a player, he turned out for Swiss clubs including St Gallen, Basel, Zurich and Grasshopper.

He became the first Liechtensteiner to play professionally in Italy with AC Arezzo before signing for Verona, Ternana and Siena.

Across 125 internationals, he became Liechtenstein’s all-time top scorer with 16 goals, including one against Scotland at Hampden in 2010, the infamous game which saw Stephen McManus ride to the rescue with a 90th-minute winner.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington welcomes upcoming manager Frick to Pittodrie.

Being the star man for an underdog may have had something to do with his upbringing. Frick’s father didn’t exactly encourage him to make it as he started out in the game.

In a recent development, he once revealed in an interview: ‘He told me: ‘There are thousands of talents like you. You won’t make it.’.

His coaching journey began eight years ago with Vaduz, who he succeeded in getting promoted to the Swiss Super League via a play-off.

According to recent reports, appointed head coach of Luzern almost five years ago, he turned the side from relegation candidates into one capable of finishing fourth inside 18 months. There followed finishes of seventh, sixth and seventh place prior to an amicable parting of the ways when his contract expired in May.

Although Frick didn’t win anything, Luzern is not a club which is accustomed to doing so, with their last league title arriving in 1989.

Its supporters still strongly identified with him, though, and recognised that he often got more out of modest resources than he was entitled to.

They enjoyed his big personality – not scared to wind up opponents in the media and not shy at publicly calling out his own players when they didn’t live up to the standards he’d set.

Frick famously scored for Liechtenstein against Scotland in a 2-1 at Hampden in 2010.

When he left there at the end of last season, the supporters felt the loss of a passionate manager who wore his heart on his sleeve, had no time for egos and stopped at nothing to deliver success.

In the Granite City, he will call out anyone not giving their absolute all every moment they are in a red jersey. And unlike the diplomatic Thelin, the fireworks are likely to be seen in public.

Sources indicate that if his time at Luzern proves prescient, those who resist or disrupt the dressing room will soon be moved on. Those who do their best by him will have nothing to fear, however.

As Italian football fan Fabio Baccarini will gladly attest, although tough and demanding, Frick is also renowned as being a loyal man with a huge heart.

Baccarini, from Reggio Emilia, became fascinated by Frick in the early 2000s while collecting Panini stickers due to the fact that he played for Liechtenstein, a tiny nation he struggled to pronounce.

He wrote so many letters to his various clubs, hoping to arrange a meeting, that Frick initially feared he might be a stalker.

When they first met in 2011 after a game between Liechtenstein and San Marino, the forward presented Baccarini with a signed shirt, gave him his email address and invited him to a match in Vaduz.

And so began an extraordinary friendship which saw Baccarini regularly drive 1,000km to support the minnows and become their de facto mascot.

In a recent development, three years back, when Hibs travelled to Luzern in the Conference League, the Italian super-fan was unable to find a bed for the night. Frick ensured he got one in the team hotel at no cost.

The fresh Pittodrie boss is just the latest to follow in the footsteps of the great Sir Alex Ferguson.

As heartwarming as such tales are, it was, of course, the metrics of on-field success which drew Aberdeen to him.

Frick’s willingness to give young players a chance – another criticism made of Robinson – was a tick against his name.

He’s handed top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career. He appointed Ardon Jashari, who played against Scotland on Monday, his Luzern captain at the age of 20.

He does not appear to be wedded to a particular formation. He mostly played a 4-4-2 with a diamond at Luzern, but he’s very much a pragmatist.

When he takes his bow at Rugby Park on Saturday, he’ll select a system to suit the personnel rather than trying to shoehorn the players into a pre-ordained system.

With just two points separating their team from bottom-side Kilmarnock, how the Red Army could do with witnessing a Super Mario bounce.

Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after its worst email outage, Reuters reports

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Microsoft logo on the side of one of its office buildings.
  • Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” to change how it prevents and handles major outages, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing internal memos.
  • According to recent reports, jaspreet Singh broke the story in a Reuters exclusive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Microsoft logo on the side of one of its office buildings.

Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” to change how it prevents and handles major outages, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing internal memos. The Microsoft Code Red follows the global outage of 12 to 13 November. It knocked out Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot for about 24 hours.

According to recent reports, jaspreet Singh broke the story in a Reuters exclusive. Jason Henderson, president of M365 Core, called it the most customer-impacting incident in Exchange Online’s history. Never before had so many customers gone without email for so long, he told staff in a memo on Friday. The outage hit governments from Australia and Japan to the US, delayed trading firms, and disrupted airline communications.

“Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote, according to Reuters.

Amanda Silver oversees M365 Core and Work IQ as a corporate vice-president. She described the response in a separate memo on Monday. Engineers worked through a “fog of war”, she wrote. Responders sent more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats.

Diagnostic data sat in separate internal tracking systems. As a result, the team struggled to keep one shared picture of its theories and decisions, Silver wrote.

Charles Lamanna is Microsoft’s executive vice-president for Copilot, Agents and Platform. He told a Code Red review that the failed part had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures”, according to Silver’s memo.

Microsoft has blamed a dormant July defect in Windows for the outage, a scalability bug that went undetected for months. Chief executive Satya Nadella apologised publicly. Microsoft notes cyber activity and AI agents played no part.

Industry observers note that silver set out five workstreams under the Code Red, covering load shedding, splitting traffic by region, and faster recovery. Microsoft wants to resolve future incidents worldwide within an hour. It also intends to use AI agents to help engineers read system health data faster.

Henderson will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, plus weekly reviews. Substrate runs the engineering behind Microsoft 365’s core services. A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters that its teams keep working around the clock to apply the lessons learned.

Earlier this month, Henderson wrote that urgent patches to M365 Core services took too long to reach users worldwide. In one recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days. For the most urgent security complications, he wants an hour from detection to safe worldwide deployment. Microsoft is not there yet, he wrote.

Last week, Nadella noted that AI-found bugs will make outages more likely. Henderson also wrote that he had reviewed the organisational and structural problems behind the failure.

“Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday,” Henderson wrote.

Tech Report: GTA 6 is a generational masterpiece — and one of the few games I’ve given a perfect score in 16 years

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is easily the most impressive entry in the (in)famous series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is easily the most impressive entry in the (in)famous series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games. Its expansive map and myriad activities offer countless hours of crime-fueled mayhem, while the intriguing characters keep you invested in the narrative. This game was worth the wait and will arguably go down as the finest title of this console generation.

Enormous, explorable open world.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Platforms: PS5 (reviewed), Xbox Series X/SPrice: $79 / £69 / AU$129Release date: November 19, 2026Genre: Open-world action-adventure.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is the most impressive video game I’ve ever played. I’m not surprised, given Rockstar Games’ history of releasing technically proficient (and insanely profitable) titles, but the storied developers have truly outdone most other games with what they’ve accomplished here. The long wait and anticipation are more than justified.

Larger than any locale in the franchise’s history, the fictional state of Leonida is a character unto itself, evoking real-life Florida with its myriad eccentric characters and diverse locations. You explore this vast landscape alongside the game’s two protagonists, a Bonnie-and-Clyde-like couple who help keep the emotional center in place amid the chaos of the main story and side quests. Together, the narrative and open-world elements deliver an experience that keeps you hooked for hours.

It has been revealed that I’ve been a huge fan of the GTA series since GTA 3 arrived in 2001 and completely changed the gaming landscape. I had some trepidation about GTA 6, given how long we’ve waited for it and how much gaming (and the world) has changed since GTA 5was released in 2013. Thankfully, GTA 6 far exceeds my expectations and will more than likely be my favorite game of the generation. Here’s why...

GTA 6 straddles the line between the more grounded tone of GTA 4 and the over-the-top insanity of GTA 5. It’s fair to say this game feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 set in the 21st century, in both tone and theme. Given that RDR 2 is in my top 10 favorite games of all time, this is a major bonus.

According to recent reports, that Red Dead inspiration is most evident in the game’s first chapter, where we slowly learn about the two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal couple trying to build a newly introduced life. The slower-burn intro will turn off anyone who's played the arcade-y GTA Online for the past 13 years—and it’s a valid criticism, even if I personally didn’t mind it. After chapter 1, it’s full-on GTA-style mayhem.

It has been revealed that jason and Lucia have more grounded personalities than some of the wilder protagonists in older GTA titles, but the game generally does a good job of showing what motivates them and making you feel invested in their journey. Jason and Lucia balance each other, with the former more stoic and calculated and the latter more impulsive and instinctive. The characters are at their best together and feel incomplete apart. The leads’ relatively toned-down attitudes also contrast nicely with the absolutely bonkers characters they meet along the way.

Recent findings suggest that in true GTA fashion, this is a rags-to-riches criminal tale that builds with each subsequent mission. You feel the sense of progression as you move up in the world and take on bigger, more dangerous heists. Watching the protagonists evolve over the course of the story is also satisfying.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that in the Grand Theft Auto series, driving has often been a point of contention, and that hasn’t changed here. At least initially. During the first few hours, I found the driving mechanics overly sensitive and loose. It felt like I was driving on ice, especially in the beat-up jalopy Jason owns at the beginning.

Then I realized that, at least on PS5, the triggers are pressure-sensitive, and I shouldn’t just hold R2 all the way down. In fact, you can feel a bit of resistance when you depress the button halfway. When I figured this out, I was golden. Though some vehicles naturally control better and differently than others, I now have a good handle (no pun intended) on the pretty intricate driving mechanics.

In a recent development, pay & Spray shops are not only great for a quick paint job to lose the cops, but also for tuning your car’s performance for better handling. This can be expensive, so it’s best to wait until you have enough money and a car worth investing in, since you don’t want to upgrade a piece of crap. I like tuning cars because it reminds me of Rockstar’s Midnight Club racing series. And yes, you can totally add neon lights and nitrous!

Industry observers note that stealing cars is more involved than ever. While you can easily steal most cheaper or older cars, higher-end vehicles will have alarms, key fobs, and trackers. And even when you successfully jack a car, you need to hotwire it. The game doles out specific tools needed to steal various cars at specific points, so you'll need to be patient to grab the really high-end rides. Even if jacking cars requires more than a button press, the extra steps make stealing them feel more immersive.

Sources indicate that as criminals, Jason and Lucia always end up getting into gunfights—either with fellow lawbreakers or law enforcement. Though the shooting and cover mechanics aren’t as precise and responsive as a dedicated third-person shooter like Gears of War: E-Day, they’re the most refined of any previous GTA game.

Auto lock for weapons was essential in GTA 5 and RDR 2 because the free-aiming mechanics were so dodgy and imprecise. That’s not the case here, as I can easily land headshots with auto lock disabled. This game has its own version of Red Dead’s “Dead Eye,” called Focus Mode, which slows the world down so you can target specific body parts. This is crucial if you want to shoot arms or legs to disable rather than kill, especially since it ties into the game’s morality system. Jason and Lucia both have a Focus meter that drains while you’re in Focus Mode.

The cover mechanics are good but not great. I say that because while your character sticks to walls or the sides of cars you’re hiding behind, it’s too easy to snap out of cover when you try to move. Still, the mechanic works well enough most of the time, and you definitely want to stay in cover during intense shootouts with gang members or the police.

In a recent development, you have access to all manner of handguns, shotguns, assault rifles, and more, which you can purchase from Ammu-Nation, pilfer from dispatched enemies, or find in the open world. Like cars, you can modify weapons. Of course, buying upgrades that improve handling, extend magazine capacity, add scopes, and more can get expensive, but it’s well worth it given the number of insane shootouts you’ll encounter during the story or out in Leonidas.

It has been revealed that sticking up pawn shops and robbing banks has always been fun in GTA, but it’s even more enjoyable now with two protagonists. I never get tired of watching how shop owners and customers react when Jason and Lucia bust in with guns drawn. While one makes sure no one tries anything funny, the other threatens the clerk into emptying the register. Sometimes someone tries to be a hero and stop you, so you have to stay on your guard.

That scenario is for small shops, but if you want to break into a bank, you’ll need to prepare. Scoping out a place, either from the inside or outside, to locate exits and where the goods are kept is crucial to pulling off a successful heist. And don’t forget to have a getaway vehicle nearby, as the cops will arrive quickly if alarms are triggered (though you can always try to disable them).

Sources indicate that along the way, you’ll also discover or be told where gangs hang out or where other criminal activity occurs. These locations often have jewelry, drugs, or other contraband that you can then sell to a fence for a significant haul. As with bank robberies, you’ll want to scope out a location to identify entry points and other opportunities to exploit.

It has been revealed that the wanted system is more intricate than before. Committing crimes in a specific area raises your wanted level by up to six stars, with each star bringing more heat from law enforcement. You can drive to another county to lose the heat, but the cops will remember your vehicle, face, hairstyle, clothing, and that there were two of you. To really lose the cops, you’ll need to change your clothes, repaint your car, or temporarily split up.

In a recent development, for example, I got a 4-star wanted rating after a robbery went wrong. I drove my car deep into the woods and got out, using the trees for cover to avoid being spotted by helicopters. After finding a truck depot, I broke into a truck using a slim jim carjacking tool and stayed in the truck without turning it on. The cops swarmed the area but didn’t find me because I was lying low. After a few minutes, they left, and I drove off to change clothes and switch vehicles. None of this was scripted.

Since this is a crime game, I’m glad Rockstar updated the wanted system to feel more realistic and give you the freedom to evade the fuzz in ways not available in previous titles.

Now, I won’t go into exhaustive detail about all the side activities available. Suffice it to say that if you need a break from your criminal pursuits, there is plenty to do. That mentioned, I want to discuss some of my favorites.

Like in previous games, you can do side missions for some of the zany characters you meet. I enjoy these because they are small stories unto themselves, and also let you experience more of Leonidas’ environment and cultures. No spoilers here, but some of these side missions are completely bonkers, and sometimes quite literally out of this world.

This may sound weird, given how I neglect to do this in real life, but I’m obsessed with taking Jason and Lucia to the gym. And it’s not just because I want them to look buff and hot. For instance, lifting weights boosts your strength, making you a bit harder to kill and letting you punch enemies out more easily. Boosting your cardio lets you run and swim longer, while raising your Focus can extend your Focus Mode. You can also boost these stats by brawling, running, or eating, but I find hitting the gym more efficient and fun.

It has been revealed that you’ll also find several events that lead to missions not marked on the map. For example, you might return to your car only to find a random woman in the backseat asking for help retrieving her dog from a biker gang, or an influencer might decide to snap photos of herself with your fancy ride. This is why it pays to explore methodically, as surprises are literally around every corner.

Sources indicate that among other things, you can participate in street or boat races, get drunk and blow all your money at strip clubs, do some mud wrestling, or unwind by watching TV (the in-game TV highlights are hilarious) or doomscrolling on your phone with your partner in bed after a long day of chaos. There is no shortage of interesting activities to partake in here.

I say this without a hint of hyperbole, but GTA 6 is the most graphically impressive and detailed game I’ve ever seen. Rockstar’s proprietary RAGE Engine is in full effect, delivering awe-inspiring visuals that bring Leonida to life. Videos online can’t compare to the experience of playing GTA 6 firsthand.

The map is immense. Even at full speed on the highway, it can take five or more minutes to reach a destination. And you won’t even mind, since everything you pass is so wonderfully rendered, from distant bridges to forests beneath thick, darkening clouds. I especially love driving through Vice City at night, as the metropolis’ gleaming buildings and neon-drenched streets are a sight to behold.

It has been revealed that since Leonida is essentially a miniature version of Florida, it has similar biomes. These include muggy swamps, dense woods, and the terrifying marvel of the Caribbean Sea. As in RDR 2, the world is filled with all manner of animals, from small rats to enormous sperm whales. You can easily spend hours exploring each locale, as long as you’re wary of hungry alligators or sharks.

Humans are as intricately detailed as the animals and environments. During my playthrough, I didn’t see a single NPC who resembled another. I’m also impressed that certain character types appear only in specific neighborhoods, which adds to the realism. You can spend all day people-gazing, as the fine folks of Leonidas always have something interesting to say. But as with exploring the wilds, keep a weapon handy for when someone inevitably tries to mug you.

I played on a PS5 Pro, which, like all consoles that GTA 6 is available on, is capped at 30 frames per second. During my time, I never once saw the frame rate dip, even during intense shootouts or fast-moving chase sequences. Naturally, your experience may differ, even if you’re also playing on a PS5 Pro, but I never encountered performance issues. And though I wish we could have gotten at least 40 fps on the PS5 Pro, the locked 30 fps runs as smoothly as possible.

Beyond the gorgeous visuals, the GTA 6 experience isn’t complete without its incredible soundtrack. With over 22 radio stations featuring dozens of songs, there’s no shortage of awesome tracks to play while you commit crimes.

As before, you get a nice mix of stations featuring contemporary and classic tunes. There are also a handful of talk radio stations, which have always been a favorite of mine. Every station has an eclectic DJ or two to keep things lively. The radio stations also round out the world of GTA 6, offering entertaining insights on celebrities, famous establishments, current news, and more.

The original tunes are just as nice as the expansive licensed soundtrack. You mostly hear this music during cinematic scenes, but it also pops up when you’re fleeing the cops. There’s also a particular track from rap duo Bau-Luxe that will have you laughing out loud because of its obscene lyrics that I won’t even hint at here!

This has been one of my longer game reviews, and even it only scratches the surface of the GTA 6 experience. Suffice it to say, you can (and some will) sink countless hours into this world and still not see everything Rockstar managed to cram into it. Like an expensive drink you can buy in Vice City, this is a title you’ll want to savor, not rush.

GTA 6 is everything we could have hoped for and more. Despite a few minor quibbles, nothing here detracts significantly. I’ve never given a game I’ve reviewed at Tom’s Guide a full five stars, but if any game deserves that honor, it’s certainly GTA 6. It’s a once-in-a-generation title that shows what’s possible when you give a talented team the budget and time to craft something exceptional. GTA 6 really is that damn good!

Jetty Pro

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hypercritical

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My first two Mac apps, Front and Center and SwitchGlass, were both created back in 2020 to restore features from DragThing, the venerable Mac app that was retired in 2019.
  • After 24 years of development, DragThing had a ton of features.
  • Industry observers note that perhaps to prove them wrong, the next app I created was Hyperspace, which provided a way to reclaim disk space without removing any files.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My first two Mac apps, Front and Center and SwitchGlass, were both created back in 2020 to restore features from DragThing, the venerable Mac app that was retired in 2019. The one tiny feature that Front and Center provided was literally a single checkbox within DragThing’s preferences. SwitchGlass went a bit farther, recreating one specific kind of floating palette from DragThing (and classic Mac OS).

After 24 years of development, DragThing had a ton of features. People often joked that I was destined to slowly reimplement all of DragThing’s functionality in a series of small apps. Put another way, they were saying I was doomed to make strange little Mac apps with extremely limited appeal (and sales).

Industry observers note that perhaps to prove them wrong, the next app I created was Hyperspace, which provided a way to reclaim disk space without removing any files. Hyperspace was still a nerdy app, but at least it had somewhat broader appeal than my earlier efforts. Who doesn’t want to save disk space? But more importantly, it was totally unrelated to DragThing. I had broken the curse!

Alas, there was one more (small) thing from DragThing that I missed. I used to have a DragThing palette in the corner of my screen containing some commonly used folders. In earlier versions of macOS, it was possible to pin the Dock to a screen corner, but that wasn’t really what I wanted either. I just wanted a small, separate palette of folders in the corner.

It has been revealed that this is not a hard problem to solve. Plenty of Mac apps can provide something close to what I want…but not exactly what I want, in the specific way that I want it. For many years, I got by with some folders in the corner of my desktop. But the problem nagged at me.

Industry observers note that A few years ago, I went so far as to implement my desired feature in SwitchGlass, adding the ability to create a small, extra palette full of folders in addition to the app switcher. But it felt incongruous with the rest of the app, so I never shipped it. And I didn’t want to maintain my own private fork of SwitchGlass, so I abandoned that branch of the code.

It has been revealed that today, AI coding agents are helping to produce a bounty of new, niche Mac apps, many made by people who have little or no coding experience. Even for experienced software developers, vibe coding has made it possible to create apps that were previously “not worth building” due to an unfavorable ratio of effort to payoff.

It has been revealed that it’s in this context that I revisited my “little palette of folders” idea. Surely I could vibe-code a simple app just for me in a day or two, right?

That was three and a half months ago.

Industry observers note that so what happened? The well-known programmer’s credo comes to mind: “We do these things not because they are easy, but because we thought they would be easy.” Indeed.

Recent findings suggest that I began the project by feeding a coding agent the source code to my app, SwitchGlass, as a starting point. I wrote SwitchGlass six years ago using a substantially more primitive version of SwiftUI. (For the developers out there, it predates @Observable and @State, and it supports Macs all the way back to macOS 12 Monterey from 2021.) I asked a coding agent to modernize the code and generalize it to support an arbitrary number of palettes instead of just one app switcher palette per display.

According to recent reports, it worked, and quickly! But it was pretty shoddy. Many optimizations and niceties from SwitchGlass had been lost. So I dove in to fix them…and maybe add one or two more features, I guess….

Now, after months of work, I’ve created a bit of a monster. But in the process, I’ve fulfilled a long-held dream of mine—a dream I had set aside years ago because I thought it was impossible. I’ve replaced the Dock.

If you’ve read any of my Mac OS X reviews, you know that I’ve always been dissatisfied with the Dock. Over the past couple of decades, I’ve gotten used to it, but I still bump up against its limitations and undesirable behaviors every day. (Undesirable to me, anyway.).

To pick just one example, I’ve always wanted clicking on a folder in the Dock to open that folder in the Finder. The Dock did work this way for several years, but in 2009’s Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard (…I think?), Apple switched to requiring a Command-Option-click to open a folder in the Finder. Since then, I’ve been Command-Option-clicking folders in the Dock many, many times per day. It’s a small thing, but it adds up: seventeen years of Command-Option clicking!

But what could I do? I was forced to continue to use the Dock because there are so many things that “only the Dock can do” in macOS. I was reminded of this harsh reality when I created SwitchGlass. Why doesn’t SwitchGlass show notification badges? Why does the Calendar icon show today’s date in the Dock but not in SwitchGlass? Why don’t app icons in SwitchGlass bounce when the app needs attention? Why can’t I quit an app from SwitchGlass?

Though I did find a workaround for that last one, the answer to most of these questions is that third-party apps simply can’t do all the things the Dock can do. The Dock is part of the operating system, and it enjoys special privileges and deep integration that no third-party app can match.

Recent findings suggest that this remains true today, especially for sandboxed apps sold through the Mac App Store like SwitchGlass (and all my other Mac apps). But what about apps that aren’t in the Mac App Store? What about unsandboxed apps? How close can they come to doing all the things the Dock does, especially if they use private APIs that are forbidden in the Mac App Store?

According to recent reports, I aimed to find out. I hatched a strategy, which I confirmed on episode 706 of Accidental Tech Podcast on August 26, 2026. I would create two apps: one called Jetty that would be sold through the Mac App Store, and a more powerful, unsandboxed app called Jetty Pro that would be distributed directly to customers, outside the Mac App Store.

Recent findings suggest that but as I worked on the two apps, it became clear that “plain Jetty” was not that great. It had all the same limitations as SwitchGlass when it came to duplicating the features of the Dock. After less than two weeks of work, I abandoned plain Jetty and concentrated entirely on Jetty Pro.

Industry observers note that after three and a half months of work, there are still things that only the Dock can do, but the list is not very long. I don’t expect most users to fully replace the Dock with Jetty Pro, but I’m happily doing so. If only my 2001 self could see me now!

Recent findings suggest that now, finally, I’d like to introduce Jetty Pro: an app that creates customizable Dock-like floating palettes around the edges of your Mac’s displays. These palettes can contain any combination of files, folders, volumes, apps, Shortcuts, spacers, dividers, and even the Trash. If you’ve ever been unsatisfied with some aspect of how the the Dock works, or if you’ve just wanted to augment the Dock with some additional palettes, try Jetty Pro and make your Mac’s interface work the way you want it to. Here are some of the highlights:.

Recent findings suggest that jetty Pro palettes are extensively customizable. Nearly every palette layout metric can be adjusted. Jetty Pro can simulate the Dock backgrounds from macOS 15, 26, and 27, and it provides several of its own background appearances as well. The image at the top of this post highlights just some of the possibilities.

Jetty Pro lets you customize the icon of any item in a palette—even the Finder. And if you’ve ever wanted to break an app out of Squircle Jail, now you can do it.

In a recent development, unlike the macOS Dock, Jetty Pro will show folder label colors (without also setting a folder symbol). You can even apply color labels to folders independent of their labels in the Finder.

Don’t want to see “Running in Background” apps in macOS 27? Jetty Pro can hide them.

Want to hide notification badges for specific apps, but only in specific palettes? Jetty Pro can do that. And unlike the Dock, Jetty Pro can even hide notification badges on the System Settings app.

Jetty Pro can exclude or include running apps of your choice on a per-palette basis.

Jetty Pro lets you choose what happens when you click (or modifier-click) an app or folder in a palette.

A Jetty Pro palette can be configured to appear on a single display, selected displays, or on every display, while also choosing which attributes, like size and position, are allowed to vary per display.

It has been revealed that use Jetty Pro to augment the macOS Dock with additional palettes, or use it to replace the Dock entirely. It’s up to you.

Jetty Pro is available for a special introductory price of $9.99 per year (plus applicable taxes) until the end of 2026, with a 14-day free trial.

Download Jetty Pro 14-day Free Trial.

To learn more, including why a subscription is the only way to pay for Jetty Pro, please read the extensive documentation.

As you might have already guessed, Jetty Pro uses every private API it can get its hands on, and it requires a ton of special permissions, all of which are explained in the documentation. For sensible security reasons, macOS makes it (increasingly) cumbersome for owners to grant these permissions. But Jetty Pro needs them to do what it does. Check Settings > General in Jetty Pro and make sure it indicates “All permissions have been granted” at the bottom. If not, click the “Details…” button for further instructions.

After a brief dalliance with more “mainstream” apps like Hyperspace, I’m back to making niche apps for Mac weirdos like me. To thine own self be true, I guess. I hope there are others out there who have longed to make the Dock work just slightly differently and are now able to do so thanks to Jetty Pro.

In a recent development, I’m sure many people reading this will think it’s ridiculous that I spent months battling the limitations of macOS to create what appears (to the undiscerning eye) to be a nearly identical clone of the Dock. What a waste of time! And what took so long anyway? This is a weekend project, at most!

Sources indicate that first, I can assure you that the “simple” appearance of Jetty Pro belies the huge level of complexity and trickery required to do so many different things that macOS does not support and actively works against. If Jetty Pro really does seem simple in use, then I have done my job well. (And if you can see the seams, then that’s where I’ve failed to completely overcome a hostile system that doesn’t want to allow Jetty Pro to do what it needs to do.).

Industry observers note that second, I put a tremendous amount of time and effort into Jetty Pro. The documentation alone (which, like every word in every post on this website, was written by me and me alone) took weeks to create. During the lead up to Jetty Pro 1.0, I’ve released over 160 builds to my 250 beta testers—more than one build per day. The Jetty Pro app icon was created by the fine humans at The Iconfactory. From the start, I’ve treated Jetty Pro like a “real” app, not a throwaway vibe-coded project.

In a recent development, having spent so many years with the Dock as a tiny pebble in my shoe, the difference between it and Jetty Pro means everything to me. Like Front and Center and SwitchGlass before it, I’m now running Jetty Pro all day, every day on my Mac. Replacing the Dock with Jetty Pro has made me happier than any other app I’ve created. I hope it will make some other Mac weirdos happy too.

Things 3.25 enhancement brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (374 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro.
  • It has been revealed that say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow.
  • Industry observers note that swiping left selects a to-do.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

It has been revealed that say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Industry observers note that swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The enhancement follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

Industry News: 2035 came early

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (616 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fzakaria

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tl;dr trynix.dev boots GUI programs now.
  • I remember watching the talk The Birth & Death of JavaScript by Gary Bernhardt and falling in love with the whimsical yet dreadfully serious unfolding of the story of how JavaScript will come to dominate all software.
  • Others have noted the inevitability of JavaScript’s dominance, so perhaps it was not surprising that Atwood’s Law holds true.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tl;dr trynix.dev boots GUI programs now. Try solitaire, GL gears, xeyes, a voice, the weather over curl, or Firefox.

I remember watching the talk The Birth & Death of JavaScript by Gary Bernhardt and falling in love with the whimsical yet dreadfully serious unfolding of the story of how JavaScript will come to dominate all software.

Others have noted the inevitability of JavaScript’s dominance, so perhaps it was not surprising that Atwood’s Law holds true.

Atwood’s LawAny application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript. — Jeff Atwood, 2009.

I highly recommend watching the talk if you have not already seen it, but the short and skinny is a lookback from 2035 and how JavaScript came to be the defacto language for all software.

In Bernhardt’s retelling of events, the date is worked back from 2035, however unsurprisingly, large language models have rapidly sped up the timeline. What was once perceived to be the end-state at 2035 has arrived years earlier and you can witness it unfolding at trynix.dev.

One of the most impressive creations I’ve managed to build leveraging nixpkgs-multiverse is https://trynix.dev.

It still baffles my mind that I can run any Nix package, over 300,000 distinct package versions, straight from my browser. Truly insane capability. I was however a little dismayed at the speed of the QEMU emulation in the browser. It was slow enough that the creation tipped more towards novelty than practicality.

I woke on November 20th and saw Domen Kožar sharing a single message in our TacoSprint Discord channel: unkernel.dev.

It was the fast browser Linux experience I had sought to achieve, but with Nix.

According to recent reports, aside What is unkernel? It is Linux compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the kernel and system components to run at wasm speed while only user programs are emulated. It was published by Pooya Parsa on November 19th, 2026.

In an AI induced manic frenzy, I adopted the fresh engine along with a slough of long-wished features almost immediately.

The proof is in the pudding: unkernel delivers remarkable speed improvements over qemu-wasm,11With a very healthy set of patches applied to make it even faster. especially on first runs where kernel work dominates. The new engine is able to deliver 2x to 32x faster performance depending on the workload.22The benchmark page tracks both engines over time, measured through the real page and shell.

JavaScript & WebAssembly nirvana.

Amazingly not only does the kernel boot quickly, it also enables networking, full-fledged graphical and audio experiences directly in the browser.

Windows. A program’s Wayland surfaces are composited in the page by wland, and they float over the terminal you started them from.

GL. The VM includes a minimal Mesa build with only the virgl driver, compiled to WebAssembly, rendering through your browser’s WebGL2.

Sound. The VM has an ALSA sound card, and can play audio through your browser.

Network. curl, git clone and pip install work. Each TCP connection goes over one WebSocket to a Wisp relay.33Thank you to @_pi0_ for adding trynix.dev to his Wisp relay allow-list.

The best joke in Bernhardt’s talk is a browser running inside another browser: the Windows GIMP under Wine, in Chrome, in Firefox. Of course, I had to try it with trynix. 😈.

It has been revealed that here is Firefox in trynix, and it loading trynix.dev, and then loading Firefox again inside itself.44Do not be too overjoyed. It took more than an hour for this to render.

Sit and bask in that insanity. That is Firefox, on Linux compiled to WebAssembly, in a Firefox tab, loading the site and then loading Firefox again inside itself. 🤯.

Tech Report: Tidal Bans AI-Generated Music

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The music streaming service Tidal mentioned Tuesday that it would ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated starting next month, a move its leader believes “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”.
  • Recent findings suggest that the service will remove the AI tracks starting Dec.
  • “But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The music streaming service Tidal mentioned Tuesday that it would ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated starting next month, a move its leader believes “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”.

Recent findings suggest that the service will remove the AI tracks starting Dec. 9, making Tidal the first music streaming platform to ban AI music entirely. It comes nearly five months after Tidal noted it would demonetize any AI-powered song, force those artists to label their tracks as either AI-generated or AI-assisted and ban AI songs that were associated with “fraudulent activity,” a category that includes songs impersonating established artists and efforts to “deceive listeners.” Related Stories Amazon Debuts $30 Streaming Bundle That Includes Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece In One Place Celebrity Streaming and Commerce Platform TalkShopLive Expands to TikTok Ahead of Black Friday.

“But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done,” wrote Robert Anderson, the Tidal Lead at parent organization Block, in an X thread on Tuesday. “We’ll begin removing all wholly AI-generated tracks from our catalog, and you’ll see them completely gone by the beginning of the year.”.

Industry observers note that anderson remarked that 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays. The move will cleave the platform of 29 million tracks, Anderson added, and have it reject between 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day.

“We encourage our peers to follow suit,” he wrote.

The move comes as competitors such as Spotify and Apple Music continue to test approaches to combat the rise of AI-generated tracks proliferating on their platforms, many of which the services have labeled some version of “slop” or “spam.” Apple Music stated it would also begin labeling AI-generated or AI-assisted tracks on its platform, while Spotify said it would label artists it deemed AI creations as an “AI Persona.”.

In a recent development, spotify mentioned in a blog post last month it also removed 50 million slop or spam tracks from owners’ recommendations this year, which came after it removed 75 million of those songs from its catalog entirely. The revelation came among a number of updates regarding Spotify’s efforts to combat AI spam.

In a recent development, “This work isn’t finished,” Spotify added. “AI moves fast, and bad actors adapt just as fast. But as AI makes music more abundant, we believe listeners will value human artistry even more. Our job is to make Spotify the place they find it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 enhancement for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of upcoming features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.
  • While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.
  • According to recent reports, also: Googlebooks?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 enhancement for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of upcoming features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

According to recent reports, also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else.

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

It has been revealed that if you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome revision adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

Industry observers note that when you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

In a recent development, this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

According to recent reports, the Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

Industry observers note that the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

In a recent development, also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these latest features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the newly introduced features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually patch by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

It has been revealed that if the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the enhancement, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GreyNoise tracks threat activity using our Global Observation Grid (GOG), a sensor network designed to attract adversarial scanning and exploitation attempts on our managed infrastructure.
  • According to recent reports, we witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created.
  • The GT13 threat actor used an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GreyNoise tracks threat activity using our Global Observation Grid (GOG), a sensor network designed to attract adversarial scanning and exploitation attempts on our managed infrastructure. One might think of these sensors as conventional “honeypots,” but that doesn’t quite capture the variety, versatility, and scale at which we deploy and manage the complex fabric of the GOG. Unsolicited activity against our sensors is sketchy if not outright nefarious, and our approach allows us to capture end-to-end intrusions and analyze a broad swath of attacker infrastructure, tools, and tactics in near realtime, without waiting for lengthy incident response investigations. We fuse data from our sensor network with additional novel sources and methods to develop a comprehensive picture of adversaries.

According to recent reports, we witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created. We cannot cite all of the details here, but we can highlight observed GT13 adversary activities to illustrate their tradecraft and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).

The GT13 threat actor used an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500.

Example POST to loginSrp1 and response.

Decoded hfs_http blob from 200 OK response showing the sid that is harvested.

It has been revealed that 2026-10-05 12:21:30 UTC - A few days later, the actor used this same flow to gain access to install HFS middleware hooks that would issue commands to the compromised server. This allowed the attacker to append an SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.

In a recent development, on October 8th, we observed the actor’s automation check in to the compromised server using HFS command hook for “uname -a; df -h / | tail -1; whoami”. Then there was a lull in activity until October 19th.

Example of HFS command, which was preserved on the compromised server.

Example decoded base64 blob demonstrating that the actor was intending to download an apparent “ZULT” Linux implant to the compromised machine.

The malware download failed, and the adversary attempted to troubleshoot the download by checking running processes, invoking curl to access the resource, and viewing the network configuration.

Example of the actor following up, attempting to check on their implant.

They couldn't figure out why their implant did not download, and the actor returned the next day with a direct SSH connection to continue setting up their relay.

2026-10-20 07:22:08 UTC - The actor created a script (/root/exfil/srv_post2_.py) which set up an unauthenticated HTTP server on the hop, after which the actor began to upload files. The first exfiltrated .tgz file contained results from scan of network routes from a compromised Check Point Security Management Server, demonstrating that the actor already had access to targeted victim assets.

The actor continued to set up their environment, uploaded and installed open-source tools like Nmap and Chisel, and then set up a Chisel server as a reverse proxy.

Recent findings suggest that once the actor had the compromised server set up as a relay, they began to use it to manage their interactions with their previously compromised victim Check Point devices. There’s a lot of commingled victimology here, so we’ll refer to two sets of victims. During our visibility, the actor was actively working towards deepening their intrusion against Victim A, and we later observed bulk actions on 21 other victim Check Point devices.

Between October 20th and 26th, the adversary had one of their Victim A compromised assets download the Chisel program and run it in client mode allowing them to further scan and interact with the Victim A environment. Over the Chisel tunnel, and by using a script for CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script), the actor launched over 100 management tasks on multiple Check Point Management Servers. This included copying the firewall database and the Internal CA, minting a newly introduced certificate (pivot.p12), and unloading security policies (which would disable the firewall). Further, the actor probed Citrix Netscaler, Ivanti Connect Secure, VMware vCenter, Microsoft Exchange, Oracle TNS assets and several domain controllers.

The bulk of the adversary commands and interaction is too voluminous to dig into here, but we can expose some of the adversary’s TTPs by taking a glimpse at their tooling. The actor used at least 30 Python scripts, many of which were helpers or launchers for other scripts, and several of them were probes for vulnerabilities or runners of exploits. Excerpts are provided below to illustrate the more specialized tooling and workflows.

2026-10-20 13:54:30 UTC - First use of exploit.py against a Victim A Check Point server.

Excerpt from exploit.py -  This CVE-2026-16232 script is purportedly an adaptation of the Metasploit module for the same function. This appears to be how the actor was sending commands to the victim Check Point Security Management Servers.

2026-10-20 14:17:51 UTC - spray_portal.py used to scan another Check Point server in the Victim A environment.

Excerpt from spray_portal.py - note that this contained common/default/weak passwords, and those apparently tailored for the victim.

2026-10-21 00:34:51 UTC - The actor could not get the second compromised Check Point device to report back to the hop, so they created and launched pull_.py to steal the data from the second Check Point server and save it on the first compromised server, which could help exfiltrate the data back to the hop server.

Sources indicate that excerpt from pull_.py - The actor named this script after their targeted device. The script runs exploit_socks.py which runs exploit.py for CVE-2026-16232, enabling the actor to harvest data from the second compromised Check Point device through the first, to the hop box. Notice that this steals credentials, internal CA files, and firewall configuration.

2026-10-21 02:56:38 to 06:34:40 UTC - The actor runs broad port scanning using curl, telnet, nmap scripts, a domain controller probe and other tools for internal reconnaissance.

2026-10-21 06:39:24 to 11:28:04 UTC - The actor uses exploit scripts against multiple target servers in the Victim A environment.

2026-10-21 11:41:21 UTC - The actor uses comb.py, ssh_comb.py and ssh_spray.py to scan a variety of targets in Victim A’s network. Note that these scripts contain usernames and passwords that were themed to the target victim. The actor either knew or was guessing names and passwords that the target might use.

Recent findings suggest that 2026-10-26 02:17:30 UTC - The actor issued a bulk certificate managing task to 24 compromised Check Point Security Manager servers including those belonging to Victim A and 21 other victim assets. The results of this task were shipped back to the hop server in a text file. We did not observe the actor sending this command task to these devices, indicating that it was issued from another part of the adversary’s infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that note that these text files contained the victim IP addresses and were in incrementing IP order, indicating an automation looped through them to run the commands on the compromised Check Point servers, and deliver them via scp to this exfil folder. Each file was delivered from victim infrastructure, showing that each of the compromised devices hold the SSH private key that matches the public key planted on the hop.

Industry observers note that all of these files contain error messages which indicate that the certificate task failed. Though we did not see follow-on attempts, the task information and IP addresses from these outputs were enough for us to identify and notify many of the victim organizations either directly or through government partners.

Excerpt from sample /root/exfil/pc_XXX-XXX-XXX-XXX.txt.

One of the error messages had a preload error for /usr/lib/.libproc.so registered in /etc/ld.so.preload, which may indicate an implant on the device.

After the certificate minting failures, the actor’s activity dropped again until November 2nd.

2026-11-02 02:28:27 UTC - By early November, other threat actors had begun to scan and attempt to abuse the compromised server. We observed the GT13 actor use a script to perform a self-check for a Linux IPv4 use-after-free bug (CVE-2026-98432). After the check, the actor attempted to patch the system using Linux’s own command-line tool nftables to drop IPv4 packets with IP options that may trigger the bug. This allowed the actor to protect their hop from others engaging in future exploitation of the bug.

According to recent reports, example commands of the actor testing a CVE-2026-98432 script on the hop box, and then attempting to patch the vulnerability with nftables, the built-in Linux firewall and packet-filtering framework. You’ll notice the patching commands happened rapidly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov.
  • Sources indicate that google has unveiled that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini.
  • To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Sources indicate that google has unveiled that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

Sources indicate that if you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that claims “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

Sources indicate that A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get consumers familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

Recent findings suggest that when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

In a recent development, additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google indicates. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the newly introduced feature more comparable.

Tech Report: Microsoft states its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two fresh frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
  • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model highlights 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
  • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two fresh frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model highlights 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

Recent findings suggest that this doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

According to recent reports, it’s also notable to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft highlighted slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

In a recent development, one thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the organization paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

Sources indicate that there’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

In a recent development, this becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft confirmed MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

According to recent reports, think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the firm itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a tech giant is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

It has been revealed that A firm with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

According to recent reports, A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

In a recent development, there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft claims the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

In a recent development, benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open matter.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these fresh models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.
