As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

In a recent development, portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Recent findings suggest that forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's new full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

Industry observers note that they are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The newly introduced national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

In a recent development, his form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

But it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

It has been revealed that the attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

Industry observers note that he was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he said: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the major-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

It has been revealed that 'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the aims, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

In a recent development, he was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

By the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

According to recent reports, if Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

Recent findings suggest that 'Today is a dream come true,' he said after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

In a recent development, after 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of fresh manager Jorge Jesus.

When pressed if he was the latest permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a big, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

Recent findings suggest that it remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
  • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," noted Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

In a recent development, gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

It has been revealed that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

The Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the aims.

Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "substantial toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

It has been revealed that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

According to recent reports, the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah noted. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

According to recent reports, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah mentioned. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Sources indicate that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah mentioned in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh stated in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

Apple is kicking off a upcoming and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

Sources indicate that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

A fresh feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a upcoming feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

The upcoming app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Sources indicate that normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the fresh Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

It has been revealed that some of the upcoming features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their major-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

In a recent development, sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

According to recent reports, “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

Industry observers note that “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a major cheer from the home fans.

It has been revealed that tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

Industry observers note that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Recent findings suggest that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Industry observers note that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

According to recent reports, michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Recent findings suggest that de Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will rapidly look a lot different. There are more fresh faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that major-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his newly introduced-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow newly introduced signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

According to recent reports, his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

In a recent development, “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

It has been revealed that “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a latest project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

In a recent development, “We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] fresh players but we have to put something more.

It has been revealed that “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an crucial defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

Industry observers note that we had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

In a recent development, it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Industry observers note that really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can swiftly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Recent findings suggest that our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

It has been revealed that that’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

Industry observers note that he’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so rapidly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

In a recent development, according to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the massive spenders.

It has been revealed that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s fresh leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

According to recent reports, de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the major boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews stated: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • Recent findings suggest that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app people on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Recent findings suggest that agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google confirmed AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Breaking: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO With the US Government’s Blessing

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia revealed on Monday that ousted cofounder Jensen Huang would return to his role as CEO after he resigned earlier this month when multiple extramarital affairs became public, including one with a woman that the US intelligence community believes is a Chinese intelligence asset.
  • “The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C.
  • According to recent reports, the stunning news comes after weeks of reporting on alleged malfeasance in Huang’s personal and professional lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia revealed on Monday that ousted cofounder Jensen Huang would return to his role as CEO after he resigned earlier this month when multiple extramarital affairs became public, including one with a woman that the US intelligence community believes is a Chinese intelligence asset.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, chair of Nvidia’s board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.”.

According to recent reports, the stunning news comes after weeks of reporting on alleged malfeasance in Huang’s personal and professional lives. The scandal broke when The Latest York Times reported that Huang had a close, personal relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Then came news of a second extramarital affair, leading to Huang’s eventual resignation.

Sources indicate that previously, the board denied it would bring Huang back, despite Huang saying he would return if the board allowed it. Many names were floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including Arm CEO Rene Haas. But many tech experts said it was difficult to imagine Nvidia without Huang. Apparently, the board agreed.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress temporarily took over as interim CEO, telling investors at its recent earnings call that everything is “business as usual.” But additional reporting revealed that Huang regularly “humiliated” his direct reports, raising serious questions about his management style and the corporate culture of Nvidia, which Huang helped shape more than any other person over the past 20 years.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s stock price rose dramatically on Monday morning with the news of Huang’s return, dragging with it other chipmakers like AMD and Qualcomm and market indices including the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow, which all jumped up on Monday. It’s another sign that Nvidia, as a key tech giant in the AI industry, is a driving force behind the US and global economy.

It has been revealed that the board added that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” on the decision. President Donald Trump mentioned in a Truth Social post that Nvidia made the “correct and proper decision” to reinstate Huang, adding, “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”.

The board’s independently commissioned investigation into Huang will continue, but he will regain his seat on the board. Huang is still set to testify before the Senate’s banking committee on Dec. 3, and the SEC’s investigation into Nvidia is also still set to continue.

Recent findings suggest that calling into CNBC’s Squawk Box on Monday morning, Trump reiterated that Huang’s return is good news for the country. He called Huang a “genius,” saying, “We have to protect our geniuses … The bigger threat is losing the brainpower of a person like Jensen.” In a rambling interview, Trump talked about the importance of Nvidia’s industry-leading chips.

In a recent development, trump previously floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking over Nvidia’s top job, which gained zero traction. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pushing for further scrutiny of Huang and Nvidia’s compliance with US export control rules. While Trump loosened the rules around how US chipmakers can do business with Chinese companies, there are still bans on selling the most advanced chips.

But we need only look to the stock market to see why the Trump administration may be changing its tune. Since the beginning of the scandal, Nvidia’s stock price has fallen dramatically, wiping out billions in market value. Monday morning’s news of Huang’s return saw premarket trading hike its share price by 30%. With Nvidia, so goes the entire stock market. And after last week’s Anthropic IPO failed to quell concerns over a growing “AI bubble” — where Nvidia is smack-dab in the center — the rebound points to investors’ confidence in Huang, Nvidia and the AI industry, spies and affairs be damned.

According to recent reports, within Silicon Valley, some have continually pushed for Huang’s return. Elon Musk posted an ominous “It is done” on Monday morning; Epic CEO Tim Sweeney posted a link to AC/DC’s Back in Black, a nod to Huang’s affinity for expensive black leather jackets.

Industry observers note that the tech industry, perhaps more than any other, thrives on the narrative of the god-like startup founder. It’s why Jensen Huang was synonymous with Nvidia, Sam Altman with OpenAI and Dario Amodei with Anthropic. And this is not the first time a major tech CEO’s departure has caused such a commotion.

“[Huang’s] return may help restore investor confidence, but the upheaval echoes Sam Altman’s brief ouster and reinstatement at OpenAI,” Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne mentioned, “raising similar questions about corporate governance and the outsized influence of individual leaders over the future of AI.”.

Altman was fired and reinstated within a chaotic five-day period in 2023. The OpenAI board accused Altman of lying to them, but he was ultimately welcomed back and has kept a firm grip on the now-huge AI company ever since. This episode is the basis for Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming movie, Artificial, starring Andrew Garfield as Altman, coming out next month.

In a recent development, those tech founders have become increasingly intertwined with government power, particularly since Trump’s return to office. Many Big Tech executives, including Huang, have donated billions in personal funds for Trump’s projects, such as his inauguration fund and plans for a White House ballroom. It’s led many tech critics to argue that Big Tech is buying influence to avoid regulation and oversight.

“​For years, Major Tech has used ‘national security’ as a pretext for killing pro-competition, kids’ privacy, and AI safety bills,” said Sacha Haworth, founder and CEO of the Tech Oversight Project. “But when their favorite CEO’s indiscretion helps a foreign rival, those concerns are thrown out the window in favor of protecting their own interests.”.

Coca-Cola at $95 or PepsiCo at $140: Which Dividend King Could Turn $1,000 Into More Money by 2036?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coca-Cola (KO +2.24%) and PepsiCo (PEP +2.17%) are two of the most dependable dividend stocks investors can own.
  • Industry observers note that however, these consumer staples giants offer distinctly different investment opportunities right now.
  • With Coca-Cola stock recently at $95 and PepsiCo trading at $140 a share, here's which one could turn a $1,000 investment into more money by 2036.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 24, 2026 at 9:09AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

Coca-Cola (KO +2.24%) and PepsiCo (PEP +2.17%) are two of the most dependable dividend stocks investors can own. Both are Dividend Kings, having increased their payouts annually for more than 50 consecutive years.

Industry observers note that however, these consumer staples giants offer distinctly different investment opportunities right now. Coca-Cola is delivering stronger earnings growth, but its stock commands a substantial valuation premium. PepsiCo has struggled with slower growth, especially in North America, but offers a higher dividend yield and a lower earnings multiple.

With Coca-Cola stock recently at $95 and PepsiCo trading at $140 a share, here's which one could turn a $1,000 investment into more money by 2036.

In a recent development, coca-Cola is thriving these days. The global beverage giant reported 7% net revenue growth during the third quarter (all organic), driven in part by 5% global unit case volume growth. Meanwhile, its comparable earnings per share rose 11%. That strong showing gave the tech giant the confidence to boost its full-year outlook. Coke now expects to deliver at least 11% comparable earnings-per-share growth this year, or about $3.33 per share.

Sources indicate that with its share recently trading around $95 apiece, Coke sells for almost 29 times earnings. That's a premium price for a premium business. For comparison, the S&P 500 trades at about 20 times earnings. As a result of its high valuation, Coke's dividend yield is right now down to around 2.2%.

NYSE · As of 11:37 AM ET 11/24/26.

In a recent development, the challenge is that Coke's long-term ambition is to deliver 7%-9% comparable earnings-per-share growth. Add in its roughly 2% yield, and we're looking at 9% to 11% annualized returns, assuming the tech giant maintains its premium valuation multiple. That's a demanding outlook.

PepsiCo isn't thriving like Coke. It's facing headwinds in both its North American beverage and snack businesses. While its revenue rose 5.6% during the third quarter, organic revenue growth was only 3.1%. Meanwhile, it delivered only 1.5% growth in core earnings per share.

It has been revealed that as a result of headwinds, Pepsi cut its guidance and now expects to deliver 2.5% to 3.5% core earnings-per-share growth this year (down from 5% to 7%). That implies it will earn around $8.40 per share at the midpoint. With Pepsi stock at $140, it trades at less than 17x earnings.

NASDAQ · As of 11:38 AM ET 11/24/26.

According to recent reports, that's a much less demanding valuation multiple. It's also why the beverage and snacking giant offers a much higher current yield (4.2%). If Pepsi can turn things around and get back to its long-term growth ambition of delivering high single-digit core earnings-per-share growth, it could deliver total returns in the 11%-13% range, and that's before any valuation multiple expansion.

In a recent development, I considered a rather simple scenario for both Coke and Pepsi over the next decade. I assumed both companies would deliver 6% annual earnings-per-share growth, while Coke's valuation multiple contracts slightly to 23x, and Pepsi's expands to 19x. Under those assumptions, here's what $1,000 invested in each stock would be worth a decade from now, assuming you reinvested your dividends:.

It has been revealed that as that chart shows, PepsiCo generates the larger projected payoff. Its lower initial earnings multiple, higher starting dividend yield, and potential valuation recovery would combine to deliver a much higher total return compared to Coke. However, that assumes Pepsi eventually turns things around and starts delivering earnings growth approaching its long-term target range.

Both Coca-Cola and PepsiCo should continue rewarding shareholders with growing dividends over the coming decade. However, the price investors pay to open a position will play an important role in their total returns.

Sources indicate that while Pepsi currently has a higher stock price than Coca-Cola ($140 vs. $95), it has a much lower valuation and higher dividend yield. As a result, it could grow a $1,000 investment into around $2,850 over the next 10 years, $1,000 more than the same investment in Coca-Cola. That's why I'd favor PepsiCo at these prices.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Newly introduced data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Newly introduced data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

It has been revealed that employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

Sources indicate that “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report highlights how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Sources indicate that greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson mentioned.

It has been revealed that what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ latest top stressor.

In a recent development, it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report noted.

Industry observers note that but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

Sources indicate that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the manufacturer, human or AI,” Samson remarked. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Industry observers note that samson remarked that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

Industry observers note that “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most notable decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse noted.

In a recent development, A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse noted.

#176831. Charging to 100% Every Night Wears Down Your Phone’s Battery. Try This Instead

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1065 w)

Charging to 100% Every Night Wears Down Your Phone’s Battery. Try This Instead

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, apple claims iPhone batteries are most comfortable at temperatures between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit, and charging outside that range, whether in a hot car or inside a thick case, speeds up wear.
  • Industry observers note that voltage stress at the top of the charge range, heat from fast charging and the cumulative effects of full discharge cycles all accelerate capacity loss.
  • Age is part of it, sure, but the overnight charging habit accelerates the process considerably.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple claims iPhone batteries are most comfortable at temperatures between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit, and charging outside that range, whether in a hot car or inside a thick case, speeds up wear. Heat is one of two things that age a phone battery faster than normal use. The other is time spent at 100%. Avoiding both takes very little effort, and the charge limit settings on iPhones, Pixels and Galaxy phones handle part of the job for you. Here’s how to charge in a way that keeps your battery healthier for longer.

Industry observers note that voltage stress at the top of the charge range, heat from fast charging and the cumulative effects of full discharge cycles all accelerate capacity loss. The damage may not appear immediately, but it’s measurable after one year and obvious after two.

Age is part of it, sure, but the overnight charging habit accelerates the process considerably. Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity faster when they spend extended time at the top of their charge range, which is precisely where an overnight charge leaves them. The fix doesn’t require a fresh phone or even a new charger. It requires a small adjustment to a habit most people have never thought twice about.

Keeping a lithium-ion cell pinned at 100% creates voltage stress, and the heat generated from sitting on a charger could end up meaning the difference between keeping your current phone a little longer or having to buy a fresh one. So once and for all, does keeping your phone plugged in really hurt the battery? Here’s what the experts suggest.

In a recent development, it isn’t about immediate damage but rather how fast your battery ages over time. Understanding the difference between what will and won’t break your phone is key. Here is the truth about your charging habits.

Battery health is not just about how many times you charge your phone. It is also about how it manages voltage, temperature and maintenance. Lithium-ion batteries age fastest when they are exposed to extreme levels: 0% and 100%.

Recent findings suggest that keeping these batteries near full charge for long stretches of time puts additional voltage stress on the cathode and electrolyte. This is why many devices use “trickle charging” or temporarily pause at 100%, topping up only when needed.

Still, the biggest threat is not overcharging, but heat. When your phone is plugged in and running demanding apps, it produces heat that accelerates chemical wear inside the battery. If you are gaming, streaming or charging on a hot day, that extra warmth does far more harm than leaving the cable plugged in overnight.

The Apple battery guide describes lithium-ion batteries as “consumable components” that naturally lose capacity over time. To slow that decline, iPhones use Optimized Battery Charging, which learns your daily routine and pauses charging at about 80% until just before you typically unplug, reducing time spent at high voltage.

Apple also advises keeping devices between 0 and 35 degrees Celsius (32 and 95 degrees Fahrenheit) and removing certain cases while charging to improve heat dissipation. You can read more on the official Apple battery support page.

According to recent reports, samsung offers a similar feature called Battery Protect, found in the One UI battery and device care settings. When enabled, it caps charging at 85%, which helps reduce stress during long charging sessions.

Recent findings suggest that other Android makers like Google, OnePlus and Xiaomi include comparable options — often called Adaptive Charging, Optimized Charging or Battery Care — that dynamically slow power delivery or limit charge based on your habits. These systems make it safe to leave your phone plugged in for extended periods without fear of overcharging.

Recent findings suggest that even with these safeguards, some conditions can accelerate battery wear. As mentioned before, the most common culprit is high temperatures. Even for a short period of time, leaving your phone charging in direct sunlight, in a car or under a pillow can push temperatures into unsafe zones.

Recent findings suggest that heavy use, such as gaming or 4K video editing, while charging can also cause temperature spikes which can degrade the battery faster. And cheap, uncertified cables or adapters may deliver unstable current that stresses cells. If your battery is already several years old, it will naturally be more sensitive to this kind of strain.

There is no need to overhaul your habits, but a few tweaks can help your battery age gracefully. Start by turning on the optimization tools on your phone: Optimized Battery Charging on iPhones, Battery Protect on Samsung devices and Adaptive Charging on Google Pixels. These systems learn your routine and adjust charging speed so your phone is not sitting at 100% all night.

Sources indicate that keep your phone cool while charging. According to Apple, phone batteries perform best between 62 and 72 degrees Fahrenheit (16 to 22 degrees Celsius). If your phone feels hot, remove its case or move it to a better ventilated or shaded spot. Avoid tossing your phone under a pillow or too close to other electronics, like your laptop. Skip wireless chargers that trap heat overnight. Use quality chargers and cables from your phone manufacturer or trusted brands. Those cheap “fast-charge” kits you find online often deliver inconsistent current, which can cause long-term challenges.

Finally, try not to obsess over topping off the charge. It is perfectly fine to plug in your phone during the day for short bursts. Lithium-ion batteries actually prefer frequent, shallow charges rather than deep full cycles. There is no need to keep it between 20% and 80% all the time, but just avoid extremes when possible.

Keeping your phone plugged in overnight or on your desk all day will not destroy its battery. That is a leftover myth from a different era of tech. Modern phones are smart enough to protect themselves, and features such as Optimized Battery Charging or Battery Protect do most of the heavy lifting for you.

Sources indicate that still, no battery lasts forever. The best way to slow the inevitable is to manage heat, use quality chargers and let the software on your phone do its job. Think of it less as “babying” your battery and more as charging with intention. A few mindful habits today can keep your phone running strong for years to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

Industry observers note that the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

Sources indicate that it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

It has been revealed that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

Recent findings suggest that the reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this latest platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xiaomi has taken the wraps off its latest 18 Pro Max Android phone in Paris. I’ve had the phone for the past few weeks and have been putting the camera to the test in my beautiful home of Edinburgh, Scotland, as well as on the beautiful (and rainy) streets of Paris. You can check out my review of the phone if you’re keen to hear more about that wild rear screen on the back, but here I wanted to share some of my favorite photos I’ve taken with the phone so far.

According to recent reports, the images seen here are taken with the phone’s various built-in camera modes, largely the black and white mode, as I love the dramatic, filmic look it produces. They’re presented either as-shot or with minimal adjustments using the phone’s built-in editing tools.

According to recent reports, taken using one of the phone’s built-in color styles, I love the vibrancy in this shot. The reds really pop, while the wider angle of the main camera emphasizes the tunnel effect of the alleyway, drawing the eye to the person and their dog.

I may be spoiling the rest of the images here by saying that this is my absolute favorite shot I’ve taken, but there we go. I took this using one of the dedicated black-and-white modes, and I think the tones here are perfect. Excellent dynamic range and contrast, and just the right amount of film grain. I positioned the figure between the buildings and had the phone almost on the floor to turn the rain-soaked tiles into a reflective surface to add some drama to this scene. I then applied a wide cinematic crop in post to give it that extra edge. Lovely stuff.

Most of my favorite photos with the phone were taken using the black-and-white mode. It’s no surprise; I shoot in black and white very often on my Leica Q3 43, and I used the monochrome mode for my favorite shots with Xiaomi’s Leitzphone earlier in the year.

The phone captures excellent black-and-white photos at night, too.

Recent findings suggest that and by exposing for the bright highlights in this scene, I was able to create this stark, moody image of my handsome orange cat, Toulouse. Is he the best cat you’ve ever seen? Of course he is.

It has been revealed that back in color, this UFO that had presumably crash-landed in this Parisian market looks great in this filmic color mode. The oranges and reds pop against the other tones in this scene.

While this quick street portrait is similarly punchy.

I used manual mode here, taking full control over the white balance and exposure settings to achieve the tones I wanted. It’s a great-looking shot with excellent dynamic range. Xiaomi’s phone doesn’t appear to go too hard with its software processing either, meaning that even fine details look quite natural. Other Android phone-makers could take note.

Recent findings suggest that as with the photo of Toulouse the cat, I exposed for the highlights here, forcing the rest of the scene under this bridge into shadow. As a result, it looks moody and dramatic but crucially it also looks exactly as I hoped it would. Many phones would try to artificially lift the shadows here, which would ruin the vibe I was going for.

Industry observers note that I took this with the phone’s telephoto zoom lens, aiming to focus more on the digger as the subject and use the water for reflection. I love how this shot looks, especially in black and white, as the cloud detail behind it is especially noticeable.

While here I used the full wide angle of the main camera in order to create a lot of negative space around the figures, emphasizing the size of the building around them.

That building was Le Grande Arche in Paris and despite it being a miserably cold, wet and cloudy day I think the phone has captured a satisfyingly stark scene here.

I don’t like flying, so I distracted myself on the flight out to Paris by taking photos of things with the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, including this man having a look out of the window.

And this shot of my plane’s wing somewhere above the UK. Again, in black and white. When it looks this good, why would I choose anything else?

Sources indicate that and while we’re still in black and white, a particularly friendly pigeon. Hi, friend!

And to round us off, this dude in shades looking at a menu.

I’m genuinely really thrilled with so many of the shots I’ve taken with this phone. The black-and-white mode in particular is spectacular, and I’m looking forward to taking more shots with it over the coming weeks and months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

It has been revealed that upcoming to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is at the moment rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Recent findings suggest that hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a fresh thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s fresh Skills.

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:.

Industry observers note that “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google remarked on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

Sources indicate that for those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

According to recent reports, chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

Sources indicate that I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google confirmed that it would be rolling out latest settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this latest take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

It has been revealed that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

Pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

Industry observers note that at the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

According to recent reports, pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

According to recent reports, another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One matter that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI patch system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

Industry observers note that I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an upgrade component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

In a recent development, you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my fresh favorite free productivity suite.

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.
