Latest Update: Nothing’s AI Earbuds Will Serve as an All-in-One Conversation Recorder

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a new pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
  • The Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality.
  • The earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a new pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg. The organization confirmed via an X post that its Ear Note wireless earbuds will be available starting Dec. 8.

The Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality. While other AI earbuds have already hit the market, the Ear Note is the first to record both phone calls and in-person conversations.

The earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations. To mitigate privacy concerns, the case only records with a physical button press — a tell that could reveal when audio is being captured around the Ear Note user.

Nothing shared that the Ear Note will work with multiple popular AI agents, but the full list of compatible software has not yet been released. The Ear Note works in tandem with an app that stores recordings from the earbuds and case, creating transcriptions and summaries similar to those created by the popular Otter AI app.

The Nothing brand has developed a cult following for combining lifestyle and fashion trends in its suite of smartphones, headphones, speakers and watches.

Industry observers note that the full product lineup is built with modern hardware, but mimics warm, nearly retrofuturist design sensibilities. The blocky Ear Note charging case continues this trend while taking the company’s tech in a upcoming direction.

In the lead-up to the Ear Note’s reveal, Nothing CEO Carl Pei described the earbuds in an X post as “a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.”.

In a Bloomberg interview, Pei indicated that Nothing isn’t trying to create AI agents or software, but that the company has a “really interesting opportunity to be the hardware layer to AI.”.

In a recent development, it’s currently unclear how much the Ear Note earbuds and case will cost when they’re released next month. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the organization hasn’t settled on a price just yet. The most expensive earbuds currently available on the Nothing store cost $149.

Sources indicate that whether you’re covering your eyes, plugging your ears or slapping a timepiece on your wrist, there’s now an ever-present option to record the world around you. Multiple companies have created their own versions of smart glasses, earbuds and watches with augmented reality capabilities.

Industry observers note that now that AI is the flavor du jour, these existing features are being enhanced by upcoming ways to scan and interact with the surrounding environment. That means a lot of visual and auditory data is being recorded by wearable devices, and very rarely with the consent of all parties involved.

The most immediate risk factors are associated with video recording – public distrust of smart glasses is so widespread that they’ve colloquially been coined “pervert glasses,” as folks fear they fundamentally break an unspoken social contract by obscuring public recording from other people.

But audio recording, enabled by Apple’s latest smartwatches, the Amazon Bee, Plaud earbuds and the latest Ear Note, is also raising concerns, not least because many states require all-party consent before you can record conversations.

Industry observers note that the Ear Note’s ability to record every bit of audio, from phone calls to in-person conversations, means it will be handling more sensitive information than other AI-powered earbuds. The company will need to face new challenges to ensure security measures are in place to prevent private chats from leaking.

At the very least, it seems as though Nothing Technology is aware of these privacy risks. According to Bloomberg, the organization created a data and security team to address concerns that cropped up during the Ear Note’s development. The company has also “obtained the same privacy certifications as competing recording products and worked with law firms to assess potential risks and safeguards.”.

Pei called wearables with recording functionality a sensitive space, and said the design team was “extra careful to not take any risks.” The Ear Note earbuds and case are largely controlled by user commands, including tactile button presses that begin the recording process.

  • Sources indicate that in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News.
  • I am not mad at this decision by Samsung.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any upcoming Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.

Sources indicate that in an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News. The switch follows other cost-cutting measures that will reduce production of the tech giant’s midrange smartphone lineup while increasing its premium Galaxy S27 offerings.

I am not mad at this decision by Samsung. Annual smartwatch updates are usually iterative anyway. Take Apple, for example. Its Apple Watch Series 10, released in 2024, had the same chip as the Apple Watch Series 11, released a year later. The most recent Apple Watch, the Apple Watch Series 12, has the same battery life as the Apple Watch Series 11. I’d expect Apple to keep its upcoming sensors, which debuted on the Series 12 and Ultra 4, for its Series 13 or Ultra 5 next year.

Samsung’s Galaxy Watch 9, which debuted with a different chip and added a few more hours of battery, had the same bones as the Galaxy Watch 8.

If some of the biggest features on these smartwatches remain the same for a few years, why not change the release schedule to a biannual one?

In a recent development, also: Galaxy Watch 9 vs. Galaxy Watch 8: I’ve compared both models, here’s my advice.

Some of the most substantial updates that arrive on upcoming devices like the Galaxy Watch 9 or Apple Watch Series 12 normally arrive through software updates, which end up landing on previous watch generations upon launch as well.

By switching from an annual release cycle to a biannual one, Samsung could drum up more excitement and anticipation between launches, and be able to surprise its customers with more purchase-worthy updates.

Samsung did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Industry observers note that building a channel of AI slop isn’t a newly introduced idea. Roku recently unveiled FairgroundTV, the first free, all-AI streaming channel.

Generative AI continues to draw widespread skepticism from both local communities and everyday internet users. Fresh data centers built to power AI models have met growing grassroots resistance over their heavy energy and water footprints, while synthetic content faces mounting cultural pushback, especially from younger audiences, who have largely rejected AI-generated media as inauthentic “slop.”.

Nike (NKE +5.08%) began its investor day on Nov. 17 by pledging to spend $12 billion on dividends from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2031. On the surface, such a commitment might reassure investors who are losing confidence in the stock.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, when it became apparent that this was merely the fiscal 2026 dividend commitment being continued for another five years, investors soured on the stock again. Moreover, they have good reason to question whether the company can meet the $12 billion commitment, and here's why.

Nike unveiled its 24th consecutive payout hike last November. If it unveils another one this month, it will mark 25 years of annual dividend increases.

Furthermore, the stock is down by 80% from its all-time high in 2021, and what that does to the yield has grabbed investors' attention. With the current yearly payout of $1.64 per share, that lower stock price has raised the yield to about 4.7%.

NYSE · As of 11:38 AM ET 11/24/26.

However, the dividend cost shows why the $12 billion pledge might bode poorly for the stock. Nike spent just over $2.4 billion annually in payouts in fiscal 2026. Since that amounts to $12 billion over five years, it suggests the dividend increases may stop, which may give investors another reason to sell the stock.

Recent findings suggest that and they may question if it can even afford $12 billion. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Aug. 31), Nike reported a free cash outflow of $64 million. Also, in fiscal 2026, the free cash flow of $2.2 billion was just under the company's dividend cost.

According to recent reports, furthermore, the prospects for a recovery continue to appear dim. Analysts forecast an 8% revenue decline in fiscal 2027 and a 1% drop the next year, implying Nike will have to dip further into its $8.4 billion in liquidity to fund the payout.

In a recent development, to management's credit, it has worked to reverse its unfortunate decision to rely purely on online sales. Unfortunately, it has struggled to regain the shelf space it surrendered to competitors.

And it continues to rely on retro brands such as Air Jordan, just as aggressive competitors such as Deckers Outdoors HOKA, and footwear designed by On Holdings have offered innovative products and won over customers who might have chosen Nike in the past. Thus, unless Nike can win back some of the business it lost, its dividend remains in danger.

Industry observers note that considering the current state of the dividend, investors should assume little in the way of payout hikes. Nike's $12 billion pledge amounts to matching its fiscal 2026 dividend outlay for five more years. That suggests it will either stop increasing its dividend or, at best, the payout hikes will be very limited.

In a recent development, moreover, this comes at a time when free cash flows have fallen below the cost of the payout. With revenue on track to fall for at least the next two years, the manufacturer lacks an obvious path to reversing this trend.

According to recent reports, the one bit of good news for shareholders is that its $8.4 billion in liquidity gives it time to rebuild its competitive advantage. Nonetheless, unless Nike can regain its edge, the apparel stock's dividend will continue to be in trouble.

  • In a recent development, with Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A fresh feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

In a recent development, with Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

It has been revealed that “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic mentioned. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

The upcoming feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic noted, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

In a recent development, as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic stated.

Industry observers note that “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic said it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic stated in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

According to recent reports, also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

In a recent development, “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he stated. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz said he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the organization and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he remarked.

According to recent reports, developer platforms overall are adapting to the upcoming state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Recent findings suggest that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Sources indicate that still, that depends on the number of PRs people are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

It has been revealed that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s organization violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
  • Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
  • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s organization violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones noted in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones stated. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this organization accountable.”.

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

Grok Imagine launched on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

In a recent development, “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield remarked in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

Sources indicate that in a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX remarked that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

In a recent development, earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In a recent development, in July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The firm seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

According to recent reports, spaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing consumers to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Substantial Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the manufacturer intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a newly introduced Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber states that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

According to recent reports, starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber claims the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Industry observers note that not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

It has been revealed that uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Recent findings suggest that uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

  • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and New South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
  • Australian sport was still in shock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and New South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

Australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between New South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Sources indicate that hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

It has been revealed that the impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Industry observers note that hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

Hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

That February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

Sources indicate that 'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

According to recent reports, it was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

It has been revealed that that grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

There was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is mentioned that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

According to recent reports, owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

Owono has become a pariah. It is said that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, stated the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

In a recent development, no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

Some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. Fiscal 2026 was another important year in Central's evolution. Over the past several years, we've taken deliberate steps to improve the quality of our portfolio and simplify our operations. We've exited our independent garden channel and pet distribution businesses, rationalized SKUs, moved away from lower-margin product lines and markets, consolidated businesses, and modernized our logistics network. At the same time, we've invested in growth through acquisitions, adding TDBBS, Champion USA, and Burpee, while expanding our international opportunities through our planned acquisition of TRIXIE.

In a recent development, together, these actions have created a stronger, more focused, and more profitable Central. And we're seeing the results. Despite a more cautious consumer environment in both our industries, our underlying organic businesses grew, margins expanded, and earnings increased. Our logistics transformation is another key milestone. With our modernized network now substantially complete, we're shifting from building the infrastructure to leveraging it. Equally important, it's a strong cultural fit. Burpee will continue to operate from its Pennsylvania headquarters under its existing leadership team, preserving the entrepreneurial spirit and expertise that made the brand successful. We see significant opportunities to support Burpee's growth by leveraging Central's scale, customer relationships, and operating capabilities. Our next major opportunity is TRIXIE. We expect the transaction to close in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and initiative to fund it with cash on hand.

Recent findings suggest that TRIXIE brings an established branded portfolio, relationships with thousands of pet retailers, and a strong track record of profitable growth and innovation. Its in-house design team introduces hundreds of new products annually, and its entrepreneurial culture is a great fit with Central. Brad Smith: Thank you, Niko. Let me run through our fourth quarter and full year results in more detail and then cover our outlook. Starting with the full year, net sales were $2.9 billion, down 6%, driven primarily by the exit of our pet distribution business at the beginning of the third quarter, which lowered reported sales, but had a minimal impact on earnings since that business operated at a lower margin. Organic net sales, which exclude businesses acquired or exited in the prior 12 months, rose 1% overall, with 1% organic growth in both Pet and Garden.

In Pet, our professional business and dog treats led organic growth for the year, with share gains in both categories, supported by our continued efforts to expand distribution and innovate in our higher margin consumable businesses. In Garden, wild bird, grass seed, and fertilizer had standout years with solid share gains driven by expanded distribution, fresh product debuts, and overall strong commercial execution. E-commerce was also a real source of momentum with record results. At the same time, a few businesses faced headwinds, particularly in garden.

These included live plants where we strategically exited several unprofitable categories and markets and managed through suboptimal weather and our garden distribution business, which was impacted by a vendor's decision to sell their products directly to retailers. Non-GAAP gross profit was $990 million, down 1%, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded 150 basis points to 33.6%. Both segments had record margins. The margin gain was driven by portfolio actions and the resulting mixed improvement, as well as cost savings, partly offset by tariffs, commodity cost and freight. Importantly, much of this improvement is structural, reflecting a higher quality portfolio and productivity gains that should continue to support margins going forward.

Non-GAAP SG&A expense was $705 million, a reduction of 5%, reflecting the exit of our pet distribution business and productivity improvements, which more than offset higher investments in commercial spend, M&A, mostly related to TRIXIE, and data and AI enablement technology. As a percentage of sales, non-GAAP SG&A margin was 23.9% compared with 23.6%. The higher rate is due to that exit, as the pet distribution business carried a lower SG&A rate than the remaining portfolio. As a result, non-GAAP operating income for the year increased 8% to $285 million, and non-GAAP operating margin expanded 120 basis points to 9.7%. Both segments had a record.

According to recent reports, non-GAAP adjustments in fiscal 2026 at the operating income line had a minimal impact, as $24 million in facility closure and business exit charges were fully offset by tariff refunds. The $24 million of charges included $14 million in Pet related to the exit of a minor business and the closure of two facilities, and $10 million in Garden, primarily related to remaining costs for the closure of a distribution center and a live plants facility. Of the total charges, $2 million was recognized in Garden in the fourth quarter.

It has been revealed that the offsetting $24 million in tariff refunds included $22 million in Pet, of which $18 million was received in Q4, and $2 million of Garden, all of which was received in Q4. Below the line, non-GAAP net interest expense was $30 million, a decrease of 8%, helped by higher interest income from larger cash balances. Non-GAAP other expense was $9 million compared to $500,000 in the prior year, driven primarily by our share of initial losses from the Pet distribution partnership in Q3 and Q4 and impairments related to minority investments in Q4. As we expected, the partnership is incurring initial losses as it executes its initial integration looks. Non-GAAP net income totaled $186 million, up 7%.

It has been revealed that non-GAAP adjustments for the full year reduced net income by $2 million. This was due to a gain in other income realized during the third quarter from the contribution of our pet distribution business to the upcoming partnership and additional interest income received in the fourth quarter from tariff refunds. We delivered record GAAP earnings per share of $3.03, up $0.48, and record non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.27, above our most recent guidance of $2.85 and last year's performance. Adjusted EBITDA for the year was $387 million, an increase of $16 million, with margin expanding by 130 basis points to 13.2% from 11.9%. Our effective tax rate for the year was 24.5%, roughly in line with the prior year.

According to recent reports, now, turning to the fourth quarter. Net sales were $537 million, down 21%, driven by the exit of our Pet distribution business. Organic net sales were down 6% with declines in both segments. Non-GAAP gross profit for the quarter was $182 million, a decrease of $15 million, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded 480 basis points to 33.9%. The margin improvement was driven by favorable mix, reflecting the exit of Pet distribution and a strategic shift away from lower margin products in Garden distribution, live plants, and private label pet beds toward higher margin categories, including packet seeds, professional, and aquatics consumables. Continued productivity gains also contributed to margin improvement, partially offsetting higher material and freight costs.

According to recent reports, non-GAAP SG&A expense for the quarter decreased 14% to $171 million. The drivers are consistent with our full year variance explanations, cost reductions from the exit of Pet distribution, and continued productivity improvements, which more than offset incremental commercial, M&A and investments in data and AI enablement technology. As a percentage of net sales, it was 31.9% compared with 29.2% given the removal of Pet distribution from our portfolio, which historically operated at a lower SG&A expense ratio. Non-GAAP operating income for the quarter was $11 million, compared with a loss of $600,000, with non-GAAP operating margin improving to 2% from negative 0.1%. Below the line, non-GAAP net interest expense was $6 million, a decrease of $1 million.

Non-GAAP other expense for the quarter was $7 million compared with $600,000, driven primarily by our share of initial losses from the pet distribution partnership and the impairment of minority investments in Q4. As a result, non-GAAP net loss for the quarter was $2 million compared with $5 million in the prior year quarter. GAAP earnings per share was $0.19, up $0.35, and non-GAAP loss per share was $0.04, an improvement of $0.05. Lastly, adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $36 million, an increase of $10 million. Now, let me provide highlights from the fourth quarter from our two segments starting with Pet.

In a recent development, net sales for the Pet segment were $305 million, a decrease of 29%, while pet organic sales were down 5%, reflecting softer consumer demand in certain categories, lost distribution in lower margin pet beds, and a temporary supply constraint in one of our businesses. While sales were down, we held or gained market share in dog treats, equine, flea and tick, and in our professional portfolio. In addition, e-commerce sales grew high single digits, driven by strong consumer engagement across online retailers and the investment we've made in building out our digital capabilities. Non-GAAP operating income was $33 million, up $2 million, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 350 basis points to 10.7%.

The increase was due to the Pet distribution exit, combined with gross margin improvements, which more than offset higher SG&A expense. Adjusted EBITDA for the segment was $42 million, up $1 million. Now, moving to Garden. Net sales for the Garden segment were $232 million, a decrease of 7% due to unfavorable weather for live plants and lower sales in garden distribution resulting from a vendor's decision to sell directly to retailers. Overall, we continue to grow share in wild bird, grass seed, and fertilizer and resumed share growth in Q4 in packet seeds. Garden e-commerce POS accelerated in the fourth quarter, growing more than 30% with record digital penetration.

We continue to see significant runway for online growth going forward. Non-GAAP operating income increased $5 million to $6 million, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 220 basis points to 2.6%, primarily driven by improved mix and productivity savings, which more than offset SG&A investments. Adjusted EBITDA increased $5 million to $16 million, with margin expanding 240 basis points to 6.9%. Now, turning to cash and balance sheet. We continue to generate solid cash flow, supporting investment in the business and M&A. Free cash flow was $271 million, a $20 million decrease from last year, as we lapped relatively larger working capital improvements.

CapEx was $45 million, an increase of $3 million, driven by prudent investments primarily in productivity-enhancing initiatives and essential maintenance projects. Depreciation and amortization was $81 million, down $4 million. At year end, cash and cash equivalents increased $210 million to a record high of approximately $1.1 billion. Total debt was $1.2 billion, unchanged from the prior year. Gross leverage ended the year at 2.6x, below our target of 3 to 3.5x. Net leverage was 0.2x, supported by our solid cash position, and we had no borrowings outstanding under our credit facility at year end. This balance sheet strength gives us the flexibility to invest in growth and in our portfolio.

M&A remains our absolute number one priority for capital allocation, and we will remain disciplined. Funding Burpee and TRIXIE with cash on hand requires no latest debt, and we expect minimal impact on gross and net leverage. As a reminder, we also purchased approximately $22 million of stock in the first half of the year and $128 million remains available under our authorizations. Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, and as Niko mentioned earlier, we are guiding full-year non-GAAP EPS to $2.65 or better.

In a recent development, our outlook incorporates the full year impact of the exit of our pet distribution business, as well as the acquisitions of Burpee, which closed at the beginning of the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and TRIXIE, which we expect to close in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. While purchase accounting is expected to limit the EPS contribution from both acquisitions in fiscal 2027, we anticipate a more meaningful earnings contribution in fiscal 2028, as these impacts moderate.

As Niko noted, our guidance reflects a prudent view of the consumer and retail environment, including continued softness and consumer demand in some Pet categories, a competitive and promotional retail landscape, select distribution losses, concentrated and lower margin product lines, and elevated retailer inventories in certain categories entering the year. We are also planning for higher fuel and oil-related costs, which we expect to be partially offset through continued productivity improvements and selective pricing actions.

Despite these near-term headwinds, we remain confident in the underlying strength of our businesses and our ability to execute against our strategic priorities, and will continue investing in areas that we believe will drive sustainable, profitable growth, including increased commercial investment and product innovation to strengthen our market positions and accelerate growth in higher margin categories and building data and AI capabilities to improve productivity, enhance decision-making, and create lasting competitive advantage. Importantly, we believe these actions together with our ongoing portfolio improvements and the expected contributions from our recent acquisitions position us well for solid future growth in fiscal 2028 and beyond.

Recent findings suggest that capital spending is expected to be approximately $50 million, up from $45 million in fiscal '26, and we anticipate continued solid cash flow generation. For the first quarter, we expect a non-GAAP loss of $0.10 to $0.15 per share, compared with earnings of $0.21 per share in the prior year quarter. A large part of the year-over-year EPS decline is driven by the inclusion of Burpee, a highly seasonal business that typically generates significant losses in the first quarter with earnings concentrated over the second and third quarters.

Industry observers note that beyond Burpee, our outlook includes softer consumer demand in certain pet categories and several timing-related factors, including elevated retailer inventories entering the quarter in a few Garden and Pet businesses and higher fuel and oil-related costs ahead of planned pricing actions. We are also working through a temporary supply constraint in one of our Pet businesses, which we expect to largely be resolved by quarter end. And we are incurring initial losses related to the ramp-up of our upcoming Pet distribution partnership. Importantly, the first quarter is typically one of our smallest and results can vary meaningfully year to year.

We expect many of these headwinds to moderate and opportunities for performance to improve as the year progresses, consistent with our full-year outlook. As always, our outlook excludes the impact of any other acquisitions, divestitures, or restructuring activities that may occur during fiscal 2027 and any further tariffs. That concludes our prepared remarks. Operator, please open the line for questions.

Industry News: The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

According to recent reports, after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-newly introduced device? (You’ve been warned.).

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

According to recent reports, the compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

Recent findings suggest that the Duo is a great gift for someone who’s stated they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV reveals on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

In a recent development, multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

Industry observers note that for the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

In a recent development, it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Industry observers note that like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Industry observers note that some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

It has been revealed that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

According to recent reports, the Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Sources indicate that A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. Industry observers note that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

It has been revealed that if PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

In a recent development, I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index demonstrated wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you initiative to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies noted Tuesday.
  • The partnership, confirmed in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
  • Industry observers note that now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies noted Tuesday.

The partnership, confirmed in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Industry observers note that now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies stated. They plan to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber aims to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

According to recent reports, “Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an important milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, stated in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

Nuro notes it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

It has been revealed that in May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the manufacturer the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

It has been revealed that uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

Recent findings suggest that it’s been a massive year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has introduced investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

New to Game Pass Premium. Previously added to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Packages Could Be at Risk of Holiday Porch Theft

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Substantial holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a plan to protect your package from porch pirates.
  • According to recent reports, CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts.
  • But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a substantial risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Substantial holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday, are here, but before you click ‘buy,’ make sure you have a plan to protect your package from porch pirates.

According to recent reports, CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent thefts. This year, the average package value is $276.24, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

But leaving your packages up for grabs could be a substantial risk — especially when thieves know holiday gifts are being delivered. On the other hand, some bad actors don’t seem to mind being caught in the act on home security cameras, so are they really enough to deter bad actors? And what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

Sources indicate that “Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other issues like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”.

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma stated that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and fresh porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

In a recent development, there are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

In a recent development, so while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to strategy how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Sources indicate that online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults blueprint to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

Industry observers note that by generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

Lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

“I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” said Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Recent findings suggest that among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

In a recent development, you shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

Recent findings suggest that “Delivery boxes have reached a new level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” stated Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”.

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

It has been revealed that home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

There are two deterrents that are keeping US adults from having security devices — cost and privacy. Findings show that 20% of US adults lack home security measures due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees. That’s followed by 9% who don’t want to use cameras because of privacy concerns.

It has been revealed that “Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” stated Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”.

If you’re looking for a camera that’s off-the-grid, consider the Arlo Go 2. It’s an LTE camera, so it uses a cellular data connection instead of Wi-Fi. It still finds a signal, supports app operation and live video viewing. If you’re looking for a power-over-Ethernet camera that uses a cable connection, the Reolink Duo 3 is a good choice.

In a recent development, lacoma added that many companies also offer ways to use local video storage and local AI detection so nothing is stored in the cloud. There are also features, such as customizable privacy zones, to minimize privacy concerns when used with the right precautions.

It has been revealed that among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

Those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

Recent findings suggest that but that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or new security devices, make a blueprint to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

In a recent development, “Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” stated Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. Newly introduced practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”.

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.
