📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

In a recent development, that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Recent findings suggest that alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

In a recent development, it was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

According to recent reports, "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

According to recent reports, “I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

Sources indicate that if there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

According to recent reports, sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

Industry observers note that it was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Industry observers note that sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

Sources indicate that “We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

Sources indicate that “We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

According to recent reports, “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa noted. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

In a recent development, arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso mentioned. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed quickly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and said it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications manufacturer - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1368 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • In a recent development, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

In a recent development, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

According to recent reports, some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s vital to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Industry observers note that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Sources indicate that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

Sources indicate that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

In a recent development, veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

It has been revealed that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Industry observers note that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

According to recent reports, apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That said, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA stated: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

England supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

According to recent reports, the issue is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel stated.

According to recent reports, 'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.
  • According to recent reports, relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial intends.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.

According to recent reports, relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial intends. That might involve asking you to lend money or your credit.

Recent findings suggest that it’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out. But it’s notable to establish boundaries so you don’t end up making a decision you’ll regret.

It has been revealed that if you suspect a money request is coming your way, think carefully about what you’re willing — and able — to offer. You might choose a specific dollar limit or to give no financial help at all.

“Only lend what you're truly OK losing,” says Alvin Carlos, a certified financial planner at District Capital Management in Washington, D.C. “Look at your budget and decide what you could hand over and never see again.”.

Choose the language that best fits your situation. Adapt your responses as needed to guide the conversation in a direction that works for you.

“I understand that you need help. I just need to review my own finances before I can give you an answer. I’ll get back to you by [day].”.

If the request comes up at a holiday or family gathering:.

“I’d rather discuss this privately. Let’s find another time to talk.”.

“Here's what I’m comfortable with, and here's what I have to protect to be financially safe, mentally safe, and to continue to be there for you in the ways that you need me.”Or, if you want to be more direct:.

Sometimes, there’s an unspoken expectation to give money because of how much loved ones think you earn, claims Ashley Agnew, a certified financial therapist in Boston.

Getting ahead of it before there's a tipping point can help with tricky dynamics, she notes.

Recent findings suggest that A recent Edward Jones report found that only about one-third of financial caregiving arrangements were planned and discussed in advance. The report also found that nearly half of financial caregivers (49%) make financial sacrifices, such as reducing or stopping saving, or tapping into their retirement account.

Factor your financial health, your values and emotional well-being into your decision:.

Review your income, expenses and savings. If you provide financial help and don’t get the money back, would you struggle to pay bills or reach financial goals? Prioritize building an emergency fund, saving for retirement and paying off high-interest debt first, Carlos states.

In a recent development, consider your relationship. Would you feel resentful if you aren’t repaid? How do you think your friend or relative would react if you decline to help? Could it damage your relationship, and if so, is it worth it?

According to recent reports, understand the credit risks. Co-signing or allowing someone else to use your credit can leave you responsible for payments and expose you to potential credit damage.

In a recent development, know the tax implications. If you’re considering a substantial gift or loan, check with a tax professional about any reporting requirements and tax consequences.

According to recent reports, consult your partner. If you share finances, make sure to include your partner in your decision-making process, Agnew indicates. If you have a parent asking for financial assistance, for example, but your cultural view is different from your spouse's, that’s a substantial opportunity for a rift.

Recent findings suggest that aim to be clear and direct. When in doubt, keep your answer concise, Agnew indicates.

“Keeping it short and sweet will communicate that you've made a decision, not that you've requested a negotiation.”.

Depending on where you left the conversation, you might have more steps to take.

Stick to your boundaries and promises. Did you offer to contribute money? Pay as agreed. Did you say no? Don’t let your friend's or family member’s persistence, or the opinions of other friends and relatives, change your mind.

If you offered to provide nonfinancial support, Carlos recommends pointing your loved one to local government and nonprofit resources. That might include emergency rent assistance, cheap or free financial advice, food banks and career services.

Document the details and set the plan in motion. If you agreed to loan money, send your relative a quick text recapping the terms, Carlos claims. He also suggests setting up a simple repayment system together, such as a recurring Zelle or Venmo transfer.

“Fewer reminders from you mean less tension,” he claims.

In a recent development, get outside help, if necessary. Despite your best efforts, it can be difficult to handle the situation on your own. If you’re feeling lingering stress or your family can’t reach a resolution, you might want to bring in some help, Agnew states.

She recommends working with a financial therapist or advisor, or using a financial wellness app.

Sources indicate that not only as we're looking to gross margin expansion, you'll notice that we have an EBITDA margin expansion. So as we go into '27, it's really how we're also improving our bottom line EBITDA. Sometimes the stabilization in gross margin may be fine given so long as we continue to improve our EBITDA margin.

Joe Giordano: As it was good to hear a little bit of the Exol revision there, customers across multiple verticals with a potential to expand to multiple sites there. Industry observers note that richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So Exol has signed up a number of customers. They haven't disclosed it or whatever for a number of reasons with the customers. But the first site, the Atlanta site is well on its way to being filled up. And that's really the test site. There's a lot of latest technology there. There's a lot of new software. We would expect -- there are 5 other sites under construction. We would expect if the Atlanta site works well that these same customers would expect to roll into the other sites. And that's what we're shooting for in the next couple of years.

Industry observers note that joe Giordano: I guess related, is there -- at what point does that -- does that $7.5 billion, is that still the right number to think about over like a medium term? Or does that get challenged in any way? Is there a time limit to when that is still enforceable?

Izilda Martins: It is $7.5 billion.

Joe Giordano: Like the initial backlog, I know it's like $11 billion now, like total backlog, but I think it was like.

Industry observers note that izilda Martins: Yes, exactly. I think the way to think of it, Joe, is there's always the potential to extend. So there's the -- as we've mentioned in the past, Exol is in the build mode, right? Think of it as of the 6 locations, one is fully sourced to C&S, the other 5 being strategically located between Atlanta, California, Chicago, Dallas and the Northeast. I think the significant news there is that we have multiple customers in Atlanta. The next site that's gone live is C&S. Give us some time to get the other, call it, 4 sites live and to see the influx of these customers and then continue or proceed with the build mode from that side.

In a recent development, joe Giordano: Okay's then just my follow-up, I'm just curious now that you're buying all these other things, right, between Fox and cellumation, like as you went through your TAM kind of analysis, I'm just curious how that's changed over time? Because like I think there's -- if we're just looking at all warehouse buildings as a starting point when we first started all talking together, maybe some of that stuff was less relevant to the core Symbotic solution, and now it's becoming like you're broadening the repertoire here.

So it's like -- I'm just curious how the interplay of what buildings -- if it's customers that just move pallets of homogenous goods versus customers that want mixed pallets, for example, like how do you think through that TAM at a more granular level now that you've broadened out and had a little bit more experience with these multiple verticals?

Industry observers note that richard (Rick) Cohen: So I think we've always understated our TAM, but I think our TAM is expanding. For instance, the e-commerce, the SymMicro, so you could use it for the back of a store. That also could be a 30,000 or 50,000 or 100,000 square foot building that's a parts supplier to auto parts, to -- because we're now doing each picking where original TAM started out as case picking to the back of the store. But for instance, we -- and Medline is a good example. So that's our first vertical into medical. We've had lots of inquiries into medical. Those are -- and many of those folks have major warehouses. And that's a combination of cases.

Industry observers note that maybe it's a case of masks or gloves that ship to a warehouse, but then there's also some very smaller, more specific items. So the ability to do both case picking and each picking. And then the third area which is the BreakPack, which we have deployed in Brooksville and now in January, we'll go live in Buckeye, Arizona. That's basically supplying drugstores and that's inner packs. So the journey that we've been on and what we're focused on is actually expanding the TAM by expanding the capabilities of customers that we can service.

And so we could now -- and for instance, we also could service restaurant supply because that's a combination of cases and eaches and we're also on the journey to eventually get into the perishable business, which is closer rather than further away. And so I think we can handle all categories pretty swiftly now. And that's why I think our TAM has always been understated, but I think it's now if you just look at e-commerce, just Walmart, the SymMicro is 400 out of 4,500 stores is $5 billion. And there's a lot of e-commerce business that's going to get done over a period of time. So I think that's a huge TAM.

The BreakPack is also a huge TAM. And then if we -- and then international, which we're now doing. So there's still people looking and it still takes a long time to get people to commit. But I think we're getting a lot more interest around the world than we had before. And over time, the more of these installations that we have, the more people become convinced of how reliable these systems are.

Operator: And our next question will come from the line of Ken Newman from KeyBanc Capital Markets.

Sources indicate that ken Newman: I wanted to follow up on the expansion of the EBITDA margin on gross margins kind of being stable comment. How do you think about the ability of leveraging the scale of the business here in the first half against -- I think you mentioned -- Rick, maybe you mentioned investing in new capabilities and R&D as a massive opportunity or target for 2027. So how do we think about your ability to lever on the SG&A line relative to the need or the want to invest in R&D and new capabilities?

In a recent development, izilda Martins: Yes. I think on the heels of the most recent acquisition, cellumation and some of the other arms, which was also in the quarter, here's how I would think about it going backwards, EBITDA up. You saw operating -- our OpEx leverage in the fourth quarter. Given what we are trying to do and all the things we're tackling, I wouldn't be expecting operating expense to stay at the levels that they were in the fourth quarter. So I would expect those to go up. But I would say high 80s is not unexpected.

According to recent reports, I would say as you look at what I guided in the first quarter, and it will probably similarly be for the first half, you could see that adjusted gross margins would stay relatively flat. So you'll still see increases in Systems revenue. Where you saw in the fourth quarter, saw a little bit of an uptick in ops services. As you know, that's lumpy quarter-over-quarter. But really, what I would say is the continuation of Systems revenue improving with stable margins, although we're leveraging our operating expenses to do all the things that will give us benefits in the future that still gets us to very, very healthy EBITDA margins.

If you look at where we ended in the year, that more than doubles where we were last year and constant increases in that EBITDA margin is what I see throughout the year. So it will be a mix between gross margin and EBITDA margin and leveraging the team we have to not only execute on what we have in front of us, but also execute on the things we want to do in the future.

According to recent reports, ken Newman: That's very helpful. I appreciate that. And then just for the follow-up, I mean, Rick, I think we've talked about -- it seems like there's still plenty of levers for you to pull in terms of latest product introductions. You talked about expanding the TAM opportunity earlier in the call. The top of your pecking order in terms of priority for new market introductions. Is it truly the opportunity from international expansion? I know we've talked about perishables and frozen and refrigerated opportunities there. Like where do you see the best opportunity in the near term and let's call it, the next 12 months?

Industry observers note that richard (Rick) Cohen: So I think still the biggest market is the U.S. where the incoming -- I think the retail world, the consumer world is expecting significant inflation, both in wages and the cost of goods over the next couple of years. So we're getting a lot of people that are looking at the opportunity and saying, over the next couple of years, with wage inflation, with upcoming contracts, we really need to be proactive here. That being mentioned, the European market is really interested in the next-generation structure because real estate is so expensive in Europe, and they're looking at if we can retrofit existing buildings.

According to recent reports, and then, of course, Walmart has put us in both North Canada and South America, Central America, and then there are some folks in Asia and that part of the world that are just looking because in some of those countries, like Fresh Zealand, Australia, there's just no labor. And so they have to automate, and we're the newest type of automation. So I think we will always continue to grow, and we're continuing to talk to a lot of people in the U.S. But I think the European and Asian markets will eventually open up to us.

Operator: And our next question will come from the line of Colin William Rusch from Oppenheimer.

Colin William Rusch: Rick, I just want to dig into your comment around customers engagement and being a little bit slow around moving from the pipeline into newly introduced sales. So yes, I guess I want to understand those dynamics and just what you're able to do in terms of moving those folks through the process a little bit faster and what they need to see are looking for in terms of the offering to start moving forward?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. I think as -- look, these are big decisions. These are $50-plus million opportunities. And so you have an interesting dynamic where there are people that are willing to invest in the future in the U.S. retail. There's people that are contracting in U.S. retail. And so I think it's a case-by-case study. There are a number of big retailers that just haven't invested much in automation. And what we're hearing from people now is we've been watching Walmart for a long time. They have a lot of money in deep pockets to do R&D, but we're going to be fast followers.

Recent findings suggest that so what I would tell you is it's a slow pace, a fast change. But I would expect over the next year or two, I think most people are going to have to automate because of tight labor and labor is going to get much more expensive.

In a recent development, colin William Rusch: Excellent. And then I appreciate the slide with upstream suppliers and the last mile. Can you talk a little bit about the technology portfolio that you guys have in place right now and where you might need to augment some of the in-house IP that you have in both the upstream and the last mile areas?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: So in the last mile, what we're developing is automated each picking, which is basically a mini warehouse for the most part in the back of the store is what we're developing. So these are -- most of the warehouses that we're automating are 500,000 square feet, 1 million square feet. What we're doing in the back of the store is 20,000 to 30,000 square feet. So there's a lot of applications, and these are much cheaper systems. They don't do as much, but many times people want a smaller system that doesn't do as much. And so we're providing the automation to do that. So we had to invent a upcoming bot.

It has been revealed that it's a similar bot, but it has a different payload. We had to upgrade the software. And our bots are becoming incredibly reliable. So if we're going to have 500 small systems around the world, that have to be incredibly reliable because it's going to be too hard to service them. So we have a remote control center here where we can actually teleop bots anywhere in the world. A bot to us becomes -- starts to look more and more like a drone where you give it software and then you can course correct it if it tells you. I mean you have to communicate and say, I have a problem because we can't see them all.

Sources indicate that but at this point, we have 20,000 bots out in the world, but I would say within, I don't know, 5 or 10 years, we could probably have 100,000. And so the ability to have that level of reliability and control and be able to control it remote is something that we developed. And also what's helped us technology-wise is, for instance, LiDAR, which is really important in some of these small systems because the bots are so close to each other. It used to be $5,000. We can now buy the same piece of equipment for $300.

And so the -- as we -- and what we have to do is invest in the technology when we -- when it's still too expensive and ride the technology wave of lower and lower pricing and then be able to implement that in our systems. So that's the technology route that we're following. We are -- with the back of the store systems, we now have frozen and perishable bots working. And that is something that we didn't have a year ago.

Operator: And next question will come from the line of Mark Trevor Delaney from Goldman Sachs.

Industry observers note that mark Trevor Delaney: First question, I was hoping to pick up on that topic around the in-store automation, SymMicro. I think last quarter, you talked about starting the first installation of your own prototype for the APD business. Can you give us a bit more of an upgrade around what you're seeing specifically with the installation? And if you think about follow-on prototypes, what that means as to when you may be able to recognize that backlog?

Sources indicate that richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So we have -- if you were to visit us in Wilmington, you would see a small prototype working, picking items, moving totes, bots running around. Our first installation site will go live in January, right after the holidays. Our second one will go live, I think, 6 months later. And then we would expect the next 20 to come fairly promptly after that, and then we would expect about 100 a year after that for many years. So the backlog recognition, I have to kind of leave that to Izzy, but I think that's sometime in the next 12 months.

Izilda Martins: That's correct.

Mark Trevor Delaney: And just to clarify, so at this point, you think there's just 2 prototypes rather than the 3 you talked about previously?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So there's 2 initial prototypes, and we've learned early on so much from those prototypes, and we have been able to run the software for the prototypes in simulations. So we've actually accelerated what the third prototype would be. And the third prototype will probably do 20 systems because I think we and Walmart are happy with the designs. And so I think there won't be 3 separate prototypes. I think there'll be one prototype. There's a second prototype. And then the third prototype is actually going to be very close to what the 400 systems we've committed to will look like.

According to recent reports, mark Trevor Delaney: Makes a lot of sense. My other question was around the expanded Walmart contract, nearly $7 billion. Can you give us a bit more color as to when you'd expect to complete shipping against that expanded backlog? I think you remarked don't expect to start shipping in fiscal '27, but any sense around when you'd be done with that?

Izilda Martins: It will be multiple years. I think the way to think about it, it will take us past the decade is really in this new program.

Operator: And our next question will come from the line of Matt J. Summerville from D.A. Davidson.

Matt J. Summerville: A couple of questions. First, is there a way to talk about your new customer funnel and the pace you now think you can add new customers? You used to talk about kind of 1 to 2, I believe, per year with the NGS. How should we think about that, number one? And is there a way to kind of quantify this is how many new customers across this many verticals we're tracking in our live funnel today maybe versus what that funnel looked like a year or two ago and how that velocity has changed? And then I have a follow-up.

Recent findings suggest that richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. That's a good question. It's a tough question for us to answer because the funnel -- the prospects we're talking to is significantly more than we were talking to a year ago. And these are all incoming. I mean these are people reaching out to us and say, I want to talk about whether this is applicable or not. I think it's a little early for us to say. I mean we could guess at it and say, yes, I think it's going to be more than 1 or 2 a year. It could be -- we'd be guessing, but I think it will be 3 to 5 a year or more.

And what we're really looking at is those 3 to 5 would have multiple applications. But it's definitely at least twice what it was a year ago.

Matt J. Summerville: That's helpful. And then maybe just a moment on capital deployment. You have $2 billion plus in cash, no debt. The stock is at $35. Are you thinking about potential share buybacks in light of the balance sheet strength? How should we be thinking about potential for more needle-moving M&A as far as the enterprise value of potential transactions? And how much revenue contribution should we see from trailing 12-month deals that you've touched on here during the call in '27?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: So let me just -- we actually had this question come up for the first time at our Board meeting, and they noted, is somebody going to ask you about that? So you're the first one to ask us about it that I know of. But as far as stock buybacks, we think there's just so much opportunity for acquisitions as a way of getting new customers and actually growing our sales. And so that's really what we're focused on. Money is not burning a hole in our pockets. We'll generate more cash this year.

But -- so I think what we're really focused on is how can we expand our sales growth through acquisition is really the question I think about the most. I think our product is good. I think we'll scale our margin. I'm just trying to figure out what is the best way to grow this business in a faster fashion. So that's the way I would talk about stock buybacks. And the rest I'll let Izzy answer.

It has been revealed that izilda Martins: Yes. I think it's exactly what Rick noted. I think your question around contribution of the acquisitions. I think that's too early to say. And we didn't talk much yet about cellumation, but the key there is to incorporate the celluveyor into our systems as well as selling them to other customers. So give us a little bit of time to figure out the contribution to our overall. For now, our focus, as I mentioned on OpEx going up, particularly in R&D, is to focus on integrating some of those acquisitions that we did this year.

Operator: Our next question will come from the line of Quinn Fredrickson from Baird.

It has been revealed that quinn Fredrickson: First one is just on the expanded Walmart master agreement. I think there was $125 million of development revenue also embedded in that. How should we think about the timing and cadence of revenue recognition for that piece? Is that also more in the outer years like the system piece? Or will there be some in '27? And if you could perhaps clarify what the development piece is related to as well?

Industry observers note that izilda Martins: So I'll take the timing and then Rick will take what it's for. So the timing of it right now is expected in the latter part of '27 as we work through it. Rick can take you through what it is we'll be working on and [ pivot ] for Walmart on that front.

According to recent reports, richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So when we actually went to Walmart and introduced the next-generation structure and then introduced all the space that was going to become available in these warehouses, we actually spent a lot of time strategically the 2 companies just talking about where we could take automation. And so the $125 million of development will be over the next couple of years, and it will be us working on research projects along with Walmart to figure out how we could do upstream e-commerce in a better fashion, how we could do a number of other products, how we could use cellumation, how we could use Fox automation.

So we have this pretty unique and wonderful relationship where we have a development program where Walmart really looks at us as a development and R&D arm for certain aspects of their business, and it costs money, and so we've asked them to fund it, and they did.

According to recent reports, quinn Fredrickson: Great. And second, I wonder if we could get more of an upgrade on BreakPack specifically. If you could just discuss what some of your key learnings have been from the first BreakPack that you're now implementing into 2.0? And any color on if these improvements are strengthening the ROI for the customer or speeding up deployment time?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So the new version of BreakPack, which we've piloted here at the ITC, we've also piloted in a second phase of Brooksville is actually much smarter -- these mini bots that we have developed are much smarter. They don't have -- they have LiDAR, they're not line following. They're much more reliable. They're faster. They're safer. And so those have been some of the innovations. And at Buckeye, we expect to see higher rates and less labor involved in doing it.

Operator: The next question will come from the line of Rob Jamieson from Needham.

Robert (Rob) Jamieson: Just first, I wonder if you could expand a little bit more on the international opportunities. I understand you can't say much about the expanded Walmart agreement. But when we think about cellumation and that acquisition and then some of the -- like what that adds on the conveyor side in terms of competitiveness over in Europe? And then as you approach the SymMicro system being certified, it feels like there's a lot more opportunities in Europe to compete against some of the more traditional ASRS systems. How should we think about that opportunity? Does that increase your potential to enter that region in the near term?

Industry observers note that richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. The answer is yes. So Europe is a very interesting market. There are -- there have been a number of German, Italian, mostly some English automation makers. ABB is Swiss and Austrian. And Europe, there -- what's slow to enter that market is they're -- I would say they're very provincial. They like using products within their own country. And so for us to enter that market, one, we wanted a presence in Europe and cellumation may not be the last one we buy in Europe. And two, we actually needed to show them that they don't always need to build a new building for automation. We call it a brownfield. So Europe is a very established automation business.

Most -- and many of the systems are old-line players like Dematic or Witron with conveyors and some 100-foot tall buildings. And so as we spent more and more time there, showing people that they can automate a 40-foot tall building or a brownfield, there's a lot of interest. Then they say, well, when are you coming to Europe and where is going to be your first installation. So we will continue to work on that market. We think once we enter that market, it will be a very big market for us. But it's -- we're just got to convince people that somebody from the U.S. can sell automation in Europe quite simply.

On the international side, in South America and even in Canada, it's very interesting because there's not a lot of automation in South America. And so the leap is what's the best automation and what automation are we going to use for the next 30 years. So even though labor is cheaper in certain parts of the world, there's a lot of it. There's less control. There's more inventory problems. And when they make -- and wages are going up very fast in the rest of the world. And so as they make the investment in automation, we're a very logical player because we're very reliable. And we've done one in Mexico. We started our second one in Mexico.

So we already have -- we may be the largest, I don't know if we are. But we're probably one of the first or second largest automation suppliers already in South America when you consider what we're automating. And we've just started with a couple of hundred million dollar buildings. So I think that's a very good opportunity for us.

Robert (Rob) Jamieson: That's very helpful. And then you have been making progress on the deployments and compressing the time line towards, I think it's a 10-month area. As you scale towards 100 or so simultaneous deployments here, what are some of the primary remaining maybe bottlenecks in the field? Is it still labor, construction management? Or is it now just kind of being more efficient on the software integration and commissioning phase?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: So one of the things that takes us the longest was actually putting up the structure and the next-generation structure goes up much faster. It's much simpler. It's much more reliable. It's actually way more complicated to build when you can build it in a factory and then it's easier to install on site. We're doing the same thing with our palletizing and depalletizing cells, taking a page out of the auto industry, where we are preassembling these things in a factory and then delivering them. So that -- those steps will allow us both to go faster and do more deployments per year.

And we're getting very focused on that just as a matter of point because when we start thinking about installing 50 or 100 SymMicros in a year, while we're installing big systems in a year, we spent a lot of time, hired a lot of people, a lot from the auto industry, some from aerospace, some from EV industry to figure out how to build and install these factories much faster.

Operator: Our next question come from the line of Guy Hardwick from Barclays.

Recent findings suggest that guy Hardwick: The 10-K reveals the RPO of $22.3 billion and 16% deliverable over the next 12 months, that implies just under $3.6 billion of revenue for systems and software. I know you don't give full year guidance, but could we -- is kind of a high level -- do you have a high level of confidence in that? And is that a sensible number for us to sort of hang our hats on for the [indiscernible] systems and software revenue, and then we could take a view on operational services?

Izilda Martins: Yes, absolutely. That is a number, obviously, that if we put the 16% and you're at year-end, that is what we expect to deliver in the fiscal year '27. One point that I would say, just starting off with the first question of the night today, I would say it's a little bit more uneven in the sense of that I would expect about 45% in the first half and 55% in the second half of the year, if that gives you a little bit more color. But yes, we do stand behind the 16% banding that we have in our 10-K.

Guy Hardwick: Okay. Just my follow-up. By my math, there's only 11 completions -- system completions in fiscal '26, well down on the previous year. And considering 2 years ago, you had 26 starts, why was it so low? And would you expect it to pick up a lot in 2027? And maybe you could give some guidance for completions and starts for '27?

Industry observers note that izilda Martins: Yes. So let me tell you a little bit of what's causing that a little bit less completions that you see. There's really never one factor that drives it. But to be a little bit more specific as to what we saw in what was completed. As you can see, it's a very complicated program. And we saw instances where given we either had latest technology or the BreakPack, for example, where the customer decided to either wait for the new technology or put the BreakPack in front of maybe another phase that we had signed at a different time. So there's really not much to look into other than what Rick just said.

Sources indicate that the timing that we control, which is when we're able to get in there, we're focusing on shortening it. The first half is really outside of our control, and that we're still getting some kinks, let's call it, out of the system. Although we don't guide to what we're expecting, what I would say is what I said earlier, I would expect the number of deployments and the number of completions in the first quarter to be very similar to what you saw in the fourth quarter.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Gregory (Greg) Palm from Craig-Hallum.

Sources indicate that gregory (Greg) Palm: In light of the Walmart expansion news, I'm just sort of curious, you've historically talked about kind of wallet share expansion or your opportunity within Walmart in light of that. Has that changed? I guess I'm assuming it's gotten bigger. So maybe how much bigger has that sort of TAM within Walmart specifically gotten?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: So it's -- so I'm going to let Walmart talk about that. But what I would tell you is -- so when you sign a $7 billion contract with Walmart, that's the second largest automation contract ever signed. The first one was the $11 billion contract we signed with Walmart. So these contracts are basically what Walmart has made a commitment and what we've done basically back and forth is Walmart stated, we want you to build out this part of our network and here's the value of that contract. And so I think as these contracts get bigger and Walmart gets more confidence in us, there's so much more to do with Walmart. There's imports.

It has been revealed that there's a whole bunch of other things that we can do. So no, I think we have a long runway yet with Walmart for things that we could do for them.

Gregory (Greg) Palm: Yes, makes sense. And then I guess, a clarification on the guide. So the calculation, 45-55, I think that implies that Q2 revenue would actually be down sequentially if we just use that RPO as the full year. Is that your intention?

Izilda Martins: No. That is not. Our intention would be that we continue to grow revenue sequentially.

Recent findings suggest that gregory (Greg) Palm: Okay. So then would that -- using that RPO number for full year, that would probably imply that, that number would be conservative then?

Izilda Martins: No. What you would have to do is also don't forget that RPO only includes systems and software. And so you'd also have to add operations services to that RPO number.

Richard (Rick) Cohen: And some of the other things that I would say is the APDs and the SymMicros are not in that number. There are still things that are not in our backlog that we will be building out for Walmart and for others.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Dushyant Ailani from Jefferies.

Sources indicate that dushyant Ailani: Just a quick one. On cellumation, is it going to be -- will you be deploying that only on new sites? Or do you think you can also retrofit existing sites as well?

Sources indicate that richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes, we can retrofit existing sites. One of the things that's very interesting with cellumation is and one of the big focuses we've had is that it makes things smaller. So it replaces both robots and conveyors. Mostly, it will be on fresh sites, but there are actually a bunch of things that we're doing to play with some adaptation of existing sites where we could deploy it. So it will be on both.

Industry observers note that dushyant Ailani: Understood. And then just one more. Just going to Exol real quick. I know we're still in early days here, but how do we think about the profitability for the JV longer term?

In a recent development, richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. I mean I think the profitability for the JV, we have to get beyond the 6 sites that we have. And I think the marginal profitability once we get the flow of customers we want is pretty solid.

Operator: Our next question comes from the line of Derek John Soderberg from Cantor Fitzgerald.

According to recent reports, derek John Soderberg: Rick, you've had at least a dozen or so live systems for a few years now. I'm curious what's the current savings per case that your systems are realizing, specifically in the distribution center?

Richard (Rick) Cohen: What was the...

Derek John Soderberg: Savings per case.

Richard (Rick) Cohen: The savings per case. It depends on the customer. So that's a good question. I really can't give you an answer because you have to get that from the customers. It's substantial enough so that depending upon the customer and some have lower operating costs in the beginning, some have much higher operating costs. But I mean, we're shooting for 3- to 5-year paybacks for our customers.

From the perspective of your customer, I think a good portion of that initial CapEx can be offset through reduction in inventory. So each system is handling, take tens of millions of cases per year really for, I would say, pennies, $0.02 or $0.03 or so. For instance, we're putting more cases on a truck than we initially thought that in many customers was not in the original model, which was purely a warehouse labor. So as that margin expands, and we're working with customers because they need us to, in many cases, write upcoming software for them, not a lot of software, but they need software changes. And so we're -- you'll see our recurring revenue go up over the next couple of years.

Richard (Rick) Cohen: Yes. So they had a pretty good group of customers. They had DHL, the German postal service. They had a number of mail sorters. They also had a couple of other sorters. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.
  • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
  • Recently news about massive tech has often pulled rates down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

Recently news about massive tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

Today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

According to recent reports, here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

In a recent development, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Recent findings suggest that lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of significant tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

It has been revealed that the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

Industry observers note that the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

In a recent development, we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three massive inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI demonstrated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

According to recent reports, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

Yeah, that was probably just me. Jason and Lucia would have to change a lot about their lifestyle to qualify (we know they're working on building credit, but having all your income be cash you can't really document is not going to work for a lender). But hey, I'm rooting for them.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

According to recent reports, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

Sources indicate that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
  • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his newly introduced club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Industry observers note that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

It has been revealed that “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

In a recent development, ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon stated: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice
