💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.
  • Sources indicate that it’s a massive list.
  • By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

Sources indicate that it’s a massive list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

In a recent development, I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) plan to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL consumers expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

Sources indicate that brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, says many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

In a recent development, “They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

While Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison says BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

“With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he claims.

Industry observers note that not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

According to recent reports, there are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

Long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

Sources indicate that pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

In a recent development, harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL tech giant doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

Sources indicate that because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

According to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL owners had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison says.

In a recent development, “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he states. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

Still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison claims, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

In a recent development, “Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he states. “There's a significant difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Industry observers note that additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Then a funny thing happened: Demand for hybrids took off, and it's fair to say that GM wasn't ready to seize the opportunity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Miller – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than General Motors ›.

General Motors (NASDAQ:GM) investors have heard plenty about the company's electric future, and also the billions in charges it (and many other auto companies) took by pumping the brakes when electric vehicles (EVs) took off more slowly than anticipated in the U.S.

Then a funny thing happened: Demand for hybrids took off, and it's fair to say that GM wasn't ready to seize the opportunity.

It has been revealed that that appears to be changing. Now, GM is preparing to bring more hybrids into its lineup. That could help it compete for customers who want better fuel economy without making the jump to an all-electric vehicle.

It has been revealed that in October, GM confirmed looks to prepare its Lansing Delta Township plant for future hybrid production. The factory currently builds the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia, although GM hasn't officially announced hybrid nameplates or launch timing. Reuters separately reported plans for hybrid versions of those three-row SUVs, citing people familiar with the matter.

For investors, the potential benefit is more than simply adding another powertrain to the next presentation slide. A hybrid could help GM retain a buyer who likes its vehicles but would otherwise visit a competitor for better fuel economy.

Recent findings suggest that toyota Motor already competes for those shoppers, and initially was one of the only automakers telling the industry to consider hybrids before going all in on EVs. Its U.S. Grand Highlander Hybrid sales reached 65,201 during the first nine months of 2026, up 34.3% year over year. That doesn't establish how many sales GM missed, but it emphasizes a segment where GM could offer its existing customers a reason to stay within its brands.

The surprise is that hybrids don't necessarily require shareholders to accept worse vehicle economics, as you might assume. Rival Ford Motor Company has already offered a compelling reason to think otherwise.

Recent findings suggest that two years ago, at a Bernstein conference, Ford CEO Jim Farley noted: "Many of our hybrids in the U.S. are now more profitable than their non-hybrid equivalent.".

Farley explained that customer pricing had begun covering the additional hybrid cost, something Ford hadn't achieved a year earlier. Obviously, adding a battery and electric motor adds expense. But if buyers value the fuel savings or additional capabilities enough to pay for them, the vehicle economics can absolutely work for automakers.

That changes the discussion from reluctantly offering hybrids to pursuing products customers want – which, in theory, should help protect market share without big losses generally associated with all-electric vehicles. To be fair, Farley's statement describes Ford's experience at that time, not a guarantee of GM's successful drive into more hybrid offerings. GM still has to deliver competitive products at the right cost and lure in the customers.

NASDAQ · As of 11:38 AM ET 11/24/26.

Recent findings suggest that GM isn't starting from a business where every gasoline vehicle needs rescuing, and in some cases it may have valid reasons for avoiding additional hybrid options. During its October earnings call, CEO Mary Barra stated Equinox production was already fully utilized without a hybrid.

Recent findings suggest that chevrolet Equinox. Image source: General Motors.

The opportunity is filling gaps in customer choice while earning enough to justify development and production costs. Investors would be wise to keep updated on its hybrid plans. It may need to expedite its development process to seize the opportunity before potential customers choose other brands, or before current customers leave for better options.

In a recent development, GM doesn't need to win a debate about the perfect powertrain, or produce a hybrid option for every nameplate. It needs to sell vehicles that customers want at prices that leave something worthwhile for shareholders. Over the past decade, GM has done that at nearly every opportunity. Don't be shocked if it executes similarly with its upcoming hybrids.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:33 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's fresh head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.

The Argentine was pictured greeting his new squad, with several stars having returned from international duty, before attentions turned to preparing the Red Devils for Sunday's trip to Anfield.

Pochettino also addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he prepares to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most important,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

Mauricio Pochettino took Man United first team training for the first time on Thursday.

Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez were among those to report back after international duty.

Man United will hope to hit the ground running under Pochettino when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

It has been revealed that 'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most key thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

In a recent development, 'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

In a recent development, 'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'.

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

Pochettino wants to focus on the potential of his Man United squad, rather than their current Premier League plight.

Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning.

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999.

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

According to recent reports, 'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

Sources indicate that 'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

Industry observers note that 'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

Industry observers note that 'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'.

Pochettino touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning after his overnight flight.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

Pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

Sources indicate that from there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

It has been revealed that 'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he mentioned.

'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'.

Etihad’s Fresh Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.
  • The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee).
  • They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two upcoming credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for upcoming applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

According to recent reports, elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

In a recent development, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

Sources indicate that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

According to recent reports, with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Recent findings suggest that bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

It has been revealed that however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

The earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

Sources indicate that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

Sources indicate that one of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

Recent findings suggest that there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

Sources indicate that you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s key to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jake Lerch – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 10:08AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Boeing ›.

Investors are increasingly weighing the established legacy of Boeing (BA -0.06%) against the high-growth trajectory of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -6.14%). Both companies are vying for dominance in an evolving aerospace landscape.

Boeing provides a diverse mix of commercial airplanes and defense hardware, while Space Exploration Technologies focuses on reusable rocket technology and global satellite internet. This comparison looks at their financials and risk profiles to help you decide between them.

It has been revealed that boeing remains a dominant force among defense stocks, providing critical infrastructure to government agencies and global airlines. Its defense segment relies on major contracts with the United States Department of Defense and NASA. Foreign military sales to non-U.S. nations accounted for 46% of total revenue in 2025, and this high concentration in government-related contracts adds a layer of risk to the business.

Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each organization's latest full fiscal year. In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $89.5 billion, representing a 34.5% increase compared to the previous year. Net income for the period was approximately $2.2 billion, resulting in a net margin of 2.5%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 10.0x, a metric that compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ratio of liquid assets to short-term debts, is approximately 1.2x. Free cash flow, representing cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was nearly $(1.9) billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 40% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

According to recent reports, space Exploration Technologies designs launch vehicles, spacecraft, and the Starlink satellite broadband system. The company serves a diverse market including launch services for commercial satellites and crewed spaceflight. Its rapid deployment of satellite infrastructure aims to provide high-speed internet to owners globally.

During FY 2025, the firm generated revenue of approximately $18.7 billion, representing a 33.2% year-over-year increase. Despite this growth, it reported a net loss of nearly $4.9 billion for the same period, resulting in a negative net margin of 26.4%. This compares to a net income of roughly $791.0 million in the prior fiscal year.

The December 2025 balance sheet shows a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.6x. Its current ratio is approximately 1.4x, suggesting the organization has sufficient short-term assets to meet its obligations. Free cash flow was nearly negative $14.0 billion, and note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 28.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Sources indicate that boeing faces significant operational risks related to complex manufacturing and supply chain constraints, particularly following its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems. Cost overruns on fixed-price contracts have led to substantial reach-forward losses in both defense and commercial segments. Furthermore, ongoing FAA regulatory oversight of quality control and safety systems creates uncertainty about future production rates.

Space Exploration Technologies operates in a high-risk environment where launch failures or technical setbacks could disrupt its satellite deployment and mission schedules. The company competes with established giants like Airbus (EADSF +2.56%) and Lockheed Martin (LMT +2.77%) in the global aerospace market. Rapid expansion of the Starlink network also requires continuous heavy capital investment and the navigation of complex international regulatory frameworks.

Boeing appears to have a more conservative valuation based on its Forward P/E relative to the high multiple assigned to Space Exploration Technologies.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

When comparing Boeing and SpaceX, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

It has been revealed that firstly, we should consider revenue growth. SpaceX is growing by leaps and bounds. In its most recent quarter, the company reported year-over-year revenue growth of 258%. Boeing, by contrast, has delivered average year-over-year revenue growth of about 10% over the last three years. That's certainly decent growth, but it pales in comparison to SpaceX's exceptional growth -- advantage SpaceX.

Another factor to consider is each company's profitability. Neither company has delivered consistent profits in recent quarters. However, SpaceX's operating margin did hit 2.2% in its most recent quarter. Boeing's, on the other hand, remained slightly underwater at -0.1%. While both companies hope to improve their margins going forward, SpaceX holds a slight advantage at this stage.

Industry observers note that lastly, there's valuation. Since both companies have not delivered consistent profits, we should examine their price-to-sales (P/S) ratios. SpaceX's P/S ratio is 54.1x, while Boeing's is 1.4x. In other words, SpaceX stock is massively more expensive on a price-to-sales basis. There are reasons why -- SpaceX's incredible revenue growth being the most significant -- but for those who place a high emphasis on valuation, Boeing has a big edge.

In a recent development, to sum up, both of these industrial stocks have their strengths. Boeing stock is extremely affordable, with a P/S multiple of only 1.4x. However, my choice in this head-to-head matchup is SpaceX. The company's explosive growth and its improving margins are what tip the scales in its favor.
